name: WALKING
description: Level 1 raise drill. Low-speed gait increases tissue temperature while keeping joint impact and coordination demand minimal. Use for FMS Score 1 athletes, deconditioned groups, or early sessions after time off.

name: BRISK WALKING
description: Level 2 raise drill. Faster walking raises heart rate while preserving low impact and simple gait mechanics. Use when athletes tolerate walking but are not ready for jogging or elastic contacts.

name: JOGGING
description: Level 3 raise drill. Jogging adds light impact, rhythm, and elastic foot contacts to the warm-up. Use for athletes with clean gait and no current lower-limb pain flags.

name: BACKWARD JOGGING
description: Level 4 raise drill. Backward movement changes foot strike and increases quad and posterior-chain coordination demand. Use for athletes preparing for deceleration, retreating, or defensive movement.

name: LATERAL SHUFFLES
description: Level 5 raise drill. Lateral shuffling raises temperature while introducing frontal-plane hip control and footwork rhythm. Use for field and court athletes before change-of-direction sessions.

name: SKIPPING
description: Level 6 raise drill. Skipping adds elastic timing, coordination, and higher ground-contact stiffness. Use when athletes need sprint-prep rhythm after basic locomotion is clean.

name: HIGH KNEE RUNS
description: Level 7 raise drill. High knee action increases front-side mechanics, trunk stiffness, and step frequency. Use before acceleration or speed work in athletes who maintain posture under faster contacts.

name: MULTI-DIRECTIONAL MOVEMENT SERIES
description: Level 8 raise drill. Direction changes raise temperature while exposing braking, reorientation, and coordination across planes. Use in advanced warm-ups before sport practice or open agility work.

name: JUMPING JACKS
description: Level 1 cardiovascular raise drill. Low-level bilateral contacts raise heart rate while adding simple arm-leg coordination. Use for general groups when joint tolerance and rhythm need a simple starting point.

name: LOW POGOS
description: Level 2 elastic raise drill. Low-amplitude bouncing trains ankle stiffness and short ground-contact rhythm. Use for athletes preparing the foot-ankle complex before faster jumping or sprinting.

name: FAST FEET
description: Level 3 neural raise drill. Rapid low-level contacts increase cadence, posture control, and foot placement accuracy. Use before speed or agility sessions when athletes need quickness without high impact.

name: SKATER STEPS
description: Level 4 lateral raise drill. Alternating side steps introduce frontal-plane loading and hip control without full bounding demand. Use for athletes preparing for lateral movement who are not ready for aggressive bounds.

name: LINE HOPS
description: Level 5 reactive footwork drill. Small hops over a line constrain foot placement and train quick elastic contacts. Use for athletes with stable landing mechanics who need low-level plyometric readiness.

name: POWER SKIPS
description: Level 6 potentiating raise drill. Higher-amplitude skips increase elastic stiffness, arm drive, and vertical projection. Use before sprint or jump sessions when athletes already own basic skipping rhythm.

name: REACTIVE HOPS
description: Level 7 reactive raise drill. Cue-driven hops challenge foot placement, stiffness, and fast reorganization. Use in late warm-ups before agility, plyometric, or sport-speed sessions.

name: SHORT ACCELERATIONS
description: Level 8 potentiating raise drill. Brief accelerations raise neural drive while rehearsing projection and sprint posture. Use only after movement prep is complete and the athlete shows clean mechanics.

name: 90-90 BREATHING
description: Level 1 activation drill. Supine 90-90 position fixes the pelvis and restores rib-cage position over the hips through controlled exhalation. Use for FMS Score 1–2 athletes with extension bias, poor bracing, or low-back tone.

name: DEADBUGS
description: Level 2 activation drill. Supine limb movement challenges anti-extension control while the floor gives direct spine feedback. Use for athletes who arch during warm-up drills or cannot dissociate limbs from trunk position.

name: BIRD DOGS
description: Level 3 activation drill. Contralateral reaching trains rotary stability while the trunk resists pelvic shift. Use for athletes with FMS rotary stability deficits or poor lumbopelvic control.

name: BEAR HOLDS
description: Level 4 activation drill. Hovering the knees adds closed-chain shoulder loading and trunk stiffness without locomotion. Use for athletes who need core activation before crawling, lifting, or field movement.

name: PLANKS
description: Level 5 activation drill. Full-body support trains anterior core stiffness from shoulders through hips. Use when athletes need baseline anti-extension control before loaded or dynamic work.

name: RKC PLANKS
description: Level 6 high-tension activation drill. Maximal glute, lat, and abdominal irradiation teaches deliberate bracing in short bouts. Use before strength or power sessions for athletes who leak force through the trunk.

name: BEAR CRAWLS
description: Level 7 integrated activation drill. Reciprocal crawling links shoulder stability, trunk anti-rotation, and contralateral coordination. Use for athletes who need ground-based core integration before locomotion or agility.

name: REACTIVE CORE SERIES
description: Level 8 reactive activation drill. Unplanned cues or perturbations force the trunk to stabilize without pre-set timing. Use in late warm-ups before contact, cutting, or open-skill sessions.

name: GLUTE BRIDGES
description: Level 1 glute activation drill. Supine bridging reduces balance demand while training hip extension without lumbar extension. Use for athletes who overuse the low back or fail to find glute tension in warm-ups.

name: MINI BAND BRIDGES
description: Level 2 glute activation drill. Band tension adds hip-abduction demand while the athlete maintains pelvic position. Use for athletes with valgus tendency or poor lateral hip recruitment.

name: CLAMSHELLS
description: Level 3 lateral-hip activation drill. Side-lying position isolates hip external rotation while limiting trunk compensation. Use for athletes who collapse at the knee during squat, lunge, or landing screens.

name: MONSTER WALKS
description: Level 4 gait-based activation drill. Diagonal stepping trains hip abduction and external rotation control during locomotion. Use before lower-body sessions for athletes who need better knee tracking.

name: LATERAL BAND WALKS
description: Level 5 frontal-plane activation drill. Lateral stepping loads the hip abductors while the trunk maintains level alignment. Use before cutting, shuffling, or single-leg strength work.

name: SINGLE LEG BRIDGES
description: Level 6 unilateral activation drill. Single-leg support increases hip-extension demand and exposes pelvic rotation. Use for athletes with side-to-side glute deficits or poor single-leg stance control.

name: LOADED HIP BRIDGES
description: Level 7 loaded activation drill. External load increases hip-extension demand while the floor constrains lumbar compensation. Use before heavy lower-body lifting when athletes need stronger glute drive.

name: REACTIVE GLUTE ACTIVATION
description: Level 8 reactive activation drill. Cue-driven holds, switches, or band perturbations force rapid hip stabilization. Use before sprinting, cutting, or jumping when dynamic hip control is the priority.

name: BAND PULL APARTS
description: Level 1 scapular activation drill. Band tension trains horizontal abduction and posterior shoulder engagement with low joint load. Use for athletes who sit in rounded posture or need upper-back activation before pressing.

name: WALL SLIDES
description: Level 2 scapular control drill. The wall gives feedback for upward rotation, rib control, and overhead reach. Use for athletes who flare the ribs or shrug during overhead warm-up drills.

name: SCAP PUSH UPS
description: Level 3 closed-chain activation drill. The push-up position trains scapular protraction and retraction without elbow motion. Use for athletes who lack serratus control before pressing or crawling work.

name: SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 4 hanging scapular drill. The hang trains depression and upward-rotation control under bodyweight traction. Use for athletes preparing for pull-ups, climbing, or overhead pulling.

name: FACE PULLS
description: Level 5 scapular retraction drill. External rotation and retraction under band or cable tension bias posterior shoulder control. Use before pressing or throwing sessions for athletes with anterior shoulder dominance.

name: Y-T-W SERIES
description: Level 6 multi-angle scapular drill. Multiple arm angles train lower trap, mid trap, and rotator cuff coordination. Use for athletes who need scapular control across overhead and horizontal positions.

name: BAND OVERHEAD STABILIZATION
description: Level 7 overhead activation drill. Band tension challenges the shoulder to stabilize while the trunk controls rib flare. Use for athletes with adequate overhead mobility before throws, snatches, or overhead lifts.

name: REACTIVE SHOULDER SERIES
description: Level 8 reactive shoulder activation drill. Perturbations train reflexive scapular and rotator cuff control under changing force. Use in late warm-ups for throwers, contact athletes, or overhead sport athletes.

name: ANKLE ROCKERS
description: Level 1 ankle mobility drill. Rocking shifts the tibia over the foot and restores basic dorsiflexion without load. Use for FMS Score 1 athletes who cannot access squat or lunge depth cleanly.

name: KNEE TO WALL DRILLS
description: Level 2 dorsiflexion drill. The wall provides a clear target for tibial translation while the heel stays down. Use for athletes with ankle asymmetry or early heel rise in squat and lunge screens.

name: HALF KNEELING ANKLE MOBILITY
description: Level 3 positional mobility drill. Half kneeling fixes the lead foot and constrains compensation while dorsiflexion is trained. Use when athletes need ankle range before squatting, decelerating, or split-stance work.

name: LOADED ANKLE ROCKERS
description: Level 4 loaded mobility drill. External load increases dorsiflexion demand and teaches the athlete to control end range. Use for athletes who have range passively but lose it under load.

name: DYNAMIC ANKLE MOBILITY
description: Level 5 dynamic mobility drill. Moving through ankle range while changing stance prepares the joint for gait and landing. Use before running, jumping, or multi-directional lower-body sessions.

name: HOP TO MOBILIZE
description: Level 6 elastic mobility drill. Small hops pair ankle range with stiffness and landing control. Use after basic ankle mobility is available and the athlete needs spring readiness.

name: SINGLE LEG MOBILITY DRILLS
description: Level 7 single-leg mobility drill. Single-leg stance combines ankle dorsiflexion, balance, and hip control. Use for athletes who show ankle limitation during single-leg squat, cut, or landing tasks.

name: REACTIVE ANKLE SERIES
description: Level 8 reactive mobility drill. Cue-driven hops and direction changes challenge ankle stiffness and range under unpredictable contacts. Use before advanced plyometric or agility work in athletes with clean mechanics.

name: HIP CARS
description: Level 1 hip mobility drill. Controlled articular rotations expose hip range while the pelvis stays quiet. Use for athletes with poor hip awareness or asymmetry before lower-body training.

name: QUADRUPED HIP ROCKS
description: Level 2 hip-dissociation drill. Quadruped support reduces balance demand while rocking trains hip flexion without lumbar rounding. Use for athletes who lose spine position in squat, hinge, or lunge screens.

name: WORLD'S GREATEST STRETCH
description: Level 3 integrated mobility drill. The lunge position combines hip flexor length, hamstring tension, and thoracic rotation. Use before running or field sessions when multiple mobility targets need one sequence.

name: COSSACK SQUATS
description: Level 4 frontal-plane mobility drill. The lateral squat trains adductor length, hip shift, and ankle control through a wide stance. Use for athletes preparing for lateral movement or showing adductor stiffness.

name: LATERAL LUNGES
description: Level 5 dynamic hip mobility drill. Side lunging adds frontal-plane loading and teaches hip deceleration through range. Use before cutting, shuffling, or lower-body sessions requiring lateral control.

name: SPIDERMAN MOBILITY
description: Level 6 deep-lunge mobility drill. The long lunge position loads hip extension, adductor length, and thoracic rotation. Use for athletes who need higher-range prep before sprinting, jumping, or grappling.

name: DYNAMIC HIP FLOW
description: Level 7 flow mobility drill. Linked hip positions train range transitions instead of isolated end-range holds. Use for athletes who own individual mobility drills and need warm-up efficiency.

name: ATHLETIC HIP SERIES
description: Level 8 athletic mobility drill. Sport-like hip positions combine mobility, balance, and low-level speed. Use in advanced warm-ups before change-of-direction, sprint, or skill sessions.

name: OPEN BOOKS
description: Level 1 thoracic mobility drill. Side-lying position fixes the pelvis and isolates thoracic rotation. Use for athletes with limited trunk rotation or lumbar compensation during screens.

name: QUADRUPED ROTATIONS
description: Level 2 thoracic rotation drill. Four-point support constrains the pelvis while the rib cage rotates over a stable base. Use for athletes who need trunk mobility without standing balance demand.

name: HALF KNEELING ROTATIONS
description: Level 3 hip-trunk mobility drill. Half kneeling adds pelvic control while the thoracic spine rotates. Use for athletes progressing from floor rotation to upright warm-up positions.

name: T-SPINE EXTENSIONS
description: Level 4 thoracic extension drill. The fixed support gives the thoracic spine a clear extension target while limiting lumbar compensation. Use for athletes who round through the upper back during overhead or front-rack positions.

name: STANDING ROTATIONS
description: Level 5 upright mobility drill. Standing adds foot pressure and pelvic control to active trunk rotation. Use before throwing, striking, or cutting sessions when torso rotation must transfer to sport posture.

name: MED BALL ROTATIONS
description: Level 6 loaded mobility drill. The medicine ball adds light load and intent to trunk rotation while preserving control. Use for athletes who need to bridge mobility work into rotational power prep.

name: REACTIVE ROTATIONS
description: Level 7 reactive rotation drill. Cue-driven turns train trunk rotation and repositioning without a fixed rhythm. Use before open-skill sport sessions requiring rapid torso orientation.

name: ATHLETIC ROTATION FLOW
description: Level 8 integrated rotation drill. Linked rotational positions combine hips, thoracic spine, feet, and rhythm. Use in advanced warm-ups for throwers, strikers, and field athletes.

name: ARM CIRCLES
description: Level 1 shoulder mobility drill. Small-to-large circles raise local temperature and explore shoulder range with low load. Use for athletes beginning upper-body warm-ups or returning from low-level stiffness.

name: BAND DISLOCATIONS
description: Level 2 shoulder mobility drill. The band allows adjustable assistance through shoulder flexion, abduction, and external rotation. Use for athletes who need gentle overhead range before pressing or throwing.

name: WALL ANGELS
description: Level 3 posture-control drill. The wall constrains rib flare and gives feedback for scapular upward rotation and shoulder external rotation. Use for athletes who cannot raise the arms without arching the low back.

name: SHOULDER CARS
description: Level 4 controlled mobility drill. Slow articular rotation trains active shoulder range while limiting trunk substitution. Use for athletes with shoulder range asymmetry or poor joint awareness.

name: PVC PASS THROUGHS
description: Level 5 overhead mobility drill. The PVC fixes hand spacing and guides the shoulders through a full overhead arc. Use before snatch, overhead squat, or throwing sessions when shoulder range is adequate.

name: OVERHEAD REACH SERIES
description: Level 6 integrated overhead drill. Reaching patterns link shoulder flexion, thoracic extension, and rib control. Use for athletes who need overhead prep without heavy loading.

name: DYNAMIC OVERHEAD FLOW
description: Level 7 dynamic mobility drill. Sequenced overhead positions train range transitions and scapular control under motion. Use for athletes who own static overhead mobility and need movement-ready shoulders.

name: ATHLETIC SHOULDER SERIES
description: Level 8 sport-prep mobility drill. Sport-like reaches, rotations, and catches prepare the shoulder for speed and variable angles. Use in late warm-ups for throwers, swimmers, lifters, and overhead athletes.

name: BW SQUATS
description: Level 1 squat potentiation drill. Bodyweight squats rehearse lower-body range, trunk position, and foot pressure without external load. Use after mobility work for athletes who need basic pattern readiness.

name: PRISONER SQUATS
description: Level 2 posture squat drill. Hands behind the head demand thoracic extension and trunk control during the squat. Use for athletes who fold forward or lose upper-back position.

name: GOBLET SQUATS
description: Level 3 loaded patterning drill. Anterior load provides counterbalance and encourages upright torso position. Use for athletes who need squat pattern cleanup before heavier or faster potentiation.

name: CYCLIC SQUATS
description: Level 4 rhythm squat drill. Repeated controlled reps raise tissue temperature and groove depth, tempo, and foot pressure. Use before squat or jump sessions when athletes need pattern volume without fatigue.

name: JUMP SQUATS
description: Level 5 power potentiation drill. The jump converts squat patterning into vertical force expression. Use once landing mechanics are clean and the athlete can keep knees tracking under speed.

name: BOX JUMPS
description: Level 6 reduced-impact jump drill. The box creates a target and reduces final landing drop while increasing takeoff intent. Use before power sessions when athletes need high intent with controlled landing stress.

name: REACTIVE JUMPS
description: Level 7 reactive potentiation drill. Rebound or cue-driven jumps train rapid force production with limited reset time. Use for athletes with strong landing mechanics before plyometric or sport-speed work.

name: SPORT-SPECIFIC JUMP TASKS
description: Level 8 transfer potentiation drill. Jump direction, stance, and cue match the sport task more closely than general jumps. Use in late warm-ups before practice or competition.

name: HIP HINGES
description: Level 1 hinge potentiation drill. Bodyweight hinging rehearses hip flexion with a neutral spine and loaded posterior chain position. Use for athletes who need hinge patterning before deadlifts, swings, or sprint work.

name: DOWEL HINGES
description: Level 2 corrective hinge drill. The dowel gives three-point feedback to prevent lumbar flexion or rib flare. Use for athletes who cannot maintain spine position during unloaded hinging.

name: KB DEADLIFTS
description: Level 3 loaded hinge drill. The kettlebell adds load from a centered position while keeping the pull technically simple. Use for athletes progressing from hinge patterning into loaded posterior-chain prep.

name: KB SWINGS
description: Level 4 ballistic hinge drill. The swing trains hip snap and trunk stiffness through a repeated hinge pattern. Use for athletes with clean hinge mechanics before sprinting, jumping, or power lifts.

name: POWER SWINGS
description: Level 5 higher-output hinge drill. Increased intent or load raises hip-extension power while the athlete maintains a fixed spine. Use in warm-ups for trained athletes preparing for explosive lower-body work.

name: JUMP HINGES
description: Level 6 hinge-to-jump drill. The pattern converts hip loading into vertical projection without a deep squat bias. Use for athletes who need posterior-chain power before broad jumps or acceleration work.

name: BROAD JUMPS
description: Level 7 horizontal power drill. The broad jump emphasizes hip projection, arm drive, and controlled horizontal landing. Use before acceleration sessions when athletes can brake without knee or trunk collapse.

name: REACTIVE HORIZONTAL POWER
description: Level 8 reactive horizontal drill. Cue-driven or repeated horizontal jumps train projection and braking under time pressure. Use in advanced warm-ups before sprint starts, cutting, or sport-speed tasks.

name: WALL PUSH UPS
description: Level 1 push potentiation drill. The wall reduces bodyweight load while teaching plank position and pressing mechanics. Use for FMS Score 1 athletes or early upper-body warm-ups when floor pressing is not ready.

name: INCLINE PUSH UPS
description: Level 2 push regression drill. Incline support lowers load while maintaining full-body alignment through the press. Use for athletes who need pressing pattern prep without shoulder or trunk compensation.

name: PUSH UPS
description: Level 3 foundational push drill. Full push-ups integrate trunk stiffness, scapular control, and horizontal pressing. Use before upper-body sessions when athletes can maintain body-line position.

name: EXPLOSIVE PUSH UPS
description: Level 4 upper-body power drill. Fast concentric pressing increases rate of force development while preserving trunk stiffness. Use for athletes with clean push-up mechanics before medicine ball or plyometric work.

name: MB CHEST PASSES
description: Level 5 medicine-ball power drill. The ball allows explosive horizontal pressing with release instead of joint braking. Use before pressing or contact sessions when upper-body power needs priming.

name: MB POWER PASSES
description: Level 6 integrated power drill. Higher-intent medicine ball passing links legs, trunk, and upper-body force transfer. Use for athletes who need total-body power rehearsal before sport practice.

name: PLYO PUSH UPS
description: Level 7 reactive push drill. Hand release and rapid re-contact train upper-body stiffness and fast braking. Use for advanced athletes with strong shoulder tolerance and clean landing mechanics through the arms.

name: REACTIVE UPPER BODY POWER
description: Level 8 reactive push drill. External feeds or cues force rapid pressing power under changing timing. Use in late warm-ups for contact, throwing, or court athletes.

name: BAND ROWS
description: Level 1 pull potentiation drill. Band resistance activates scapular retraction and elbow drive with low joint load. Use before pulling, throwing, or posture-heavy training sessions.

name: BAND FACE PULLS
description: Level 2 posterior-shoulder drill. The band biases retraction and external rotation while keeping load adjustable. Use for athletes who need upper-back and rotator cuff prep before pressing or throwing.

name: INVERTED ROWS
description: Level 3 bodyweight pull drill. Body angle controls load while the athlete integrates trunk stiffness and scapular control. Use for athletes who need pulling readiness before heavier rows or pull-ups.

name: EXPLOSIVE ROWS
description: Level 4 power-pull drill. Fast pulling intent trains upper-back force production while the trunk stays braced. Use before power sessions for athletes who can row without shrugging or lumbar extension.

name: MED BALL PULL APARTS
description: Level 5 dynamic posterior-chain upper drill. The medicine ball adds speed and coordination to horizontal pulling and shoulder control. Use for athletes preparing for throwing, grappling, or contact work.

name: REACTIVE ROWS
description: Level 6 reactive pull drill. Cue-driven or partner-fed rows challenge timing, scapular control, and grip response. Use when athletes need pulling mechanics under unpredictable input.

name: EXPLOSIVE PULL UPS
description: Level 7 advanced pull potentiation drill. High-velocity pulling increases neural drive while demanding strict trunk and scapular control. Use only for athletes with strong pull-up capacity and no shoulder irritation.

name: ATHLETIC PULLING SERIES
description: Level 8 transfer pull drill. Sport-like pulls combine body position, speed, grip, and trunk stiffness. Use in late warm-ups for climbing, grappling, contact, or overhead sport demands.

name: A-MARCHES
description: Level 1 locomotion potentiation drill. The march isolates posture, knee drive, and dorsiflexed foot position at low speed. Use before acceleration work for athletes cleaning up basic sprint mechanics.

name: A-SKIPS
description: Level 2 elastic locomotion drill. Skipping adds bounce and rhythm to the A-march pattern while preserving posture. Use when athletes can march cleanly but need stiffness and timing.

name: B-SKIPS
description: Level 3 cyclical mechanics drill. Lower-leg extension and recovery challenge swing-phase control without full sprint intensity. Use for athletes who overreach or lack front-side sprint control.

name: WALL DRIVES
description: Level 4 acceleration-position drill. Wall support fixes torso angle and teaches forceful ground projection through the stance leg. Use for athletes who pop upright early or push vertically during starts.

name: DRIBBLE RUNS
description: Level 5 rhythm-speed drill. Low-amplitude contacts train turnover, stiffness, and front-side mechanics. Use before sprinting when athletes need cleaner foot strike timing.

name: BUILD-UP RUNS
description: Level 6 sprint-prep drill. Gradual acceleration lets the athlete organize posture, rhythm, and relaxation before high speed. Use for athletes returning to sprint exposure or preparing for faster runs.

name: ACCELERATION RUNS
description: Level 7 acceleration potentiation drill. Short accelerations prime projection, body angle, and forceful step rhythm. Use after mobility and activation are complete before speed or field sessions.

name: REACTIVE ACCELERATION SERIES
description: Level 8 reactive speed drill. External cues train start response, projection, and re-acceleration without pre-planned timing. Use in late warm-ups for athletes preparing for sport-speed demands.

name: MOVEMENT REHEARSAL
description: Level 1 sport-specific rehearsal drill. Low-speed rehearsal grooves the session’s key movement shapes without fatigue. Use early in warm-ups when athletes need pattern exposure before technical intensity.

name: POSITIONAL DRILLS
description: Level 2 positional readiness drill. Holding and moving through sport positions trains posture, stance, and joint angles specific to the task. Use for athletes who need better setup discipline before skill work.

name: TECHNICAL DRILLS
description: Level 3 technical rehearsal drill. Slow-to-moderate technical work reinforces timing and sequencing under low physiological cost. Use before practices when movement quality must be established before speed rises.

name: DYNAMIC TECHNICAL DRILLS
description: Level 4 dynamic rehearsal drill. Adding movement speed and transitions links technique to rhythm and coordination. Use when athletes own static positions but need cleaner execution while moving.

name: SPEED TECHNICAL DRILLS
description: Level 5 speed rehearsal drill. Higher-velocity technical work raises neural drive while keeping the skill constrained. Use before sessions where speed of execution matters but full chaos is not needed.

name: REACTIVE TECHNICAL DRILLS
description: Level 6 reactive rehearsal drill. External cues force technical execution under decision demand. Use for athletes who perform well in closed drills but break down when reacting.

name: GAME SPEED DRILLS
description: Level 7 competition-speed drill. Full-speed rehearsal exposes timing, spacing, and technical control at realistic intensity. Use late in warm-ups once mobility, activation, and potentiation are complete.

name: COMPETITION READINESS DRILLS
description: Level 8 readiness drill. The drill combines sport cue, speed, intent, and execution standard to confirm the athlete is prepared to compete. Use immediately before practice or competition when the goal is final nervous-system readiness.

name: B/L WALL ASSISTED SQUAT
description: Bilateral wall assisted squat is a beginner-friendly squat variation performed by standing with your back against a wall and sliding down into a squat position while maintaining contact with the wall for support. This helps build lower body strength and proper squat form with reduced risk of falling forward.
indications_text: Ideal for beginners, those relearning squat mechanics, people with poor squat stability, early rehab

name: U/L WALL ASSISTED SQUAT
description: Unilateral wall assisted squat is a single-leg variation where you perform the squat on one leg while using the wall for balance and support, helping to address imbalances and improve unilateral strength.

name: BAND RESISTED WALL SQUATS
description: Band resisted wall squats add resistance bands around the knees or thighs to increase activation of the outer hips and glutes while performing the wall squat, promoting better knee alignment and stability.

name: WALL SUPPORTED FIG 4 SQUATS
description: Wall supported figure 4 squats involve crossing one ankle over the opposite knee (figure 4 position) while squatting against the wall, targeting hip mobility and glute stretch alongside squat strength.

name: LOADED WALL SQUATS
description: Loaded wall squats are performed by holding additional weight (e.g., dumbbells or kettlebells) while sliding down the wall into a squat hold, increasing intensity for strength building.

name: ZERCHER HOLD WALL SQUATS
description: Zercher hold wall squats involve cradling a barbell or weight in the crooks of the elbows while performing the wall squat, emphasizing core and upper back engagement.

name: STABILITY BALL WALL SQUATS
description: Stability ball wall squats place a stability ball between your back and the wall for added instability, requiring more core activation while performing the squat slide.

name: BAND ASSISTED SQUATS
description: Band assisted squats use resistance bands anchored above to provide upward assistance, making the squat easier for beginners or those building strength.
indications_text: For individuals needing added support (elderly, post-injury, post-op, or very deconditioned)

name: TRX SUPPORTED SQUATS
description: TRX supported squats use TRX straps for balance and assistance, allowing deeper squats while maintaining form and building stability.

name: PARTNER ASSISTED SQUATS
description: Partner assisted squats involve a partner providing support or resistance, helping to guide form or add challenge during the movement.

name: BAR SUPPORTED SQUATS
description: Bar supported squats use a barbell or fixed bar for hand support, aiding balance and allowing progressive loading.

name: HEEL RAISED BAND ASSISTED
description: Heel raised band assisted squats elevate the heels and use bands for assistance, targeting quads more intensely while improving ankle mobility.
indications_text: Use if athlete has limited dorsiflexion, needs quad emphasis, or struggles with trunk upright posture

name: HEEL RAISED WALL SUPPORTED SQUATS
description: Heel raised wall supported squats use the wall for back support with elevated heels, focusing on quad activation and form.

name: HEEL RAISED BW SQUAT
description: Heel raised bodyweight squats elevate the heels to emphasize quads without added weight, ideal for form practice.

name: HEEL RAISED GOBLET SQUAT
description: Heel raised goblet squats hold a weight at chest level with elevated heels, increasing quad load and stability.

name: CYCLIC SQUAT
description: Cyclic squats involve continuous reps with a rhythmic pattern, building endurance; heel raised version targets quads.

name: HEEL RAISED DB SQUAT
description: Heel raised dumbbell squats hold dumbbells with elevated heels, adding resistance for quad strength.

name: B/L BW SQUATS / PRISONER SQUATS
description: Bilateral bodyweight squats or prisoner squats place hands behind the head, emphasizing posture and core engagement.
indications_text: Universal—great for all levels, early strengthening, home exercises, warm-up routines

name: GORILLA SQUATS
description: Gorilla squats mimic gorilla posture with wide stance and hands on ground, building mobility and strength.

name: HINDU SQUATS
description: Hindu squats involve swinging arms and rising on toes at the top, adding cardio and calf work.

name: OH WALL SQUATS
description: Overhead wall squats hold arms overhead against the wall, improving posture and shoulder mobility.

name: STAGGERED STANCE BW SQUATS
description: Staggered stance bodyweight squats have one foot forward, emphasizing unilateral strength.

name: NARROW STANCE BW SQUATS
description: Narrow stance bodyweight squats bring feet close, targeting outer quads more.

name: CANDLE STICK OH SQUATS
description: Candlestick overhead squats involve rolling into squat from floor, building explosive power.

name: CYCLIC SQUATS
description: Cyclic squats maintain continuous motion, enhancing endurance.

name: SISSY SQUATS
description: Sissy squats lean back on toes, isolating quads intensely.

name: BW SUMO SQUATS
description: Bodyweight sumo squats use wide stance with toes out, targeting inner thighs.
indications_text: Use for athletes needing adductor/glute emphasis, or to address hip/knee valgus weakness

name: BANDED SUMO SQUATS
description: Banded sumo squats add band resistance for outer hip activation.

name: KB HOLD SUMO SQUATS (HANG/ GOBLET)
description: Kettlebell hold sumo squats hang or goblet hold weight, adding load.

name: DB SUMO SQUATS (HANG/ GOBLET)
description: Dumbbell sumo squats similar to KB, with hang or goblet hold.

name: BB SUMO SQUATS (HANG/ RACKED)
description: Barbell sumo squats hang or rack the bar, increasing intensity.

name: PLATE HOLD SUMO SQUATS
description: Plate hold sumo squats grip a plate at chest, similar to goblet.

name: ZERCHER HOLD SUMO SQUATS
description: Zercher hold sumo squats cradle bar in elbows, engaging core.

name: JEFFERSON HOLD SUMO SQUATS
description: Jefferson hold sumo squats straddle bar, unique grip for balance.

name: BW B/L BOX SQUATS
description: Bodyweight bilateral box squats squat to a box for controlled depth.
indications_text: Suggested for those unable to achieve low squat safely; useful to teach depth and control (post-injury return, elderly)

name: BW U/L BOX SQUATS
description: Bodyweight unilateral box squats single-leg to box, building balance.

name: BW LOW BOX SQUATS (B/L & U/L)
description: Bodyweight low box squats use lower box for deeper range.

name: KB GOBLET HOLD BOX SQUATS (B/L & U/L)
description: Kettlebell goblet hold box squats add weight for strength.

name: DB BOX SQUATS (B/L & U/L)
description: Dumbbell box squats hold DBs, increasing load.

name: BB BOX SQUATS (FRONT & BACK RACK)
description: Barbell box squats front or back rack for heavy loading.

name: OH LOADED BOX SQUATS
description: Overhead loaded box squats hold weight overhead, challenging stability.

name: DB GOBLET SQUATS
description: Dumbbell goblet squats hold DB at chest, emphasizing form.

name: BANDED B/L GLUTE BRIDGES (ASSISTED & RESISTED)
description: Level 1 corrective drill. The band provides tactile feedback at the knees, cueing abduction and preventing valgus collapse at the bottom of the bridge. Use for athletes with dormant glute medius activation or those who compensate with lumbar extension rather than hip extension. Cue: squeeze the band out while driving the hips — not the lower back — to the top.

name: BW B/L GLUTE BRIDGES
description: Level 2 foundational pattern. Removes external assistance to establish a clean bilateral hip extension under bodyweight only. Use to confirm the athlete can achieve full glute contraction and pelvic neutral without hyperextending the lumbar spine before progressing to load.

name: SL BANDED GLUTE BRIDGES
description: Level 3 unilateral activation with RNT. Single-leg position exposes left/right glute strength asymmetries; the band maintains abduction demand on the stance leg. Flag athletes who show pelvis drop or trunk rotation to the unsupported side — these require additional hip abductor work before loading.

name: SL BW GLUTE BRIDGES
description: Level 4 unilateral stability. Removes band assistance to demand full single-leg glute output with no external cue. A reliable benchmark: the athlete should hold the top position for 2–3 seconds without pelvic tilt or hamstring dominance.

name: SLANT BOARD GLUTE BRIDGES (B/L & U/L)
description: Level 5 range-of-motion overload. The slant board increases hip flexion at the start position, elongating the glute through a greater arc and demanding more strength at end-range hip extension. Use when standard bridges plateau and to address anterior pelvic tilt under fatigue.

name: LOADED GLUTE BRIDGES (KB, DB, PLATE, SB)
description: Level 6 strength progression. External load drives hypertrophy and maximal motor unit recruitment in the bilateral bridge pattern. Stability ball variation adds an anti-rotation demand to the upper body; flat load options allow heavier progression once the pattern is locked in.

name: KNEELING BANDED HINGE
description: Level 1 motor pattern drill. Kneeling removes the ankle, knee, and quad variables, isolating the hip hinge as a pure pelvis-over-fixed-spine movement. Use as the first introduction to posterior chain loading mechanics for athletes with no hinge experience or persistent lumbar substitution.

name: B/L PELVIC BRIDGE HIP THRUST (BW)
description: Level 2 pattern establishment. Elevating the shoulders onto a bench increases the range of hip extension beyond the floor bridge, biasing the glutes through full shortening. Confirm neutral spine and no rib flare at the top before loading.

name: B/L PELVIC BRIDGE HIP THRUST (LOADED)
description: Level 3 bilateral strength builder. Barbell or plate load placed over the hip crests demands controlled eccentric lowering and concentric hip drive. The most effective loaded exercise for peak glute activation per EMG research; cue athletes to drive through the heels, not the toes.

name: SL PELVIC BRIDGE HIP THRUST (BW)
description: Level 4 unilateral pattern. Single-leg hip thrust isolates glute max output and challenges anti-rotation stability of the pelvis and lumbar spine. Use to expose and correct asymmetry identified in the bilateral pattern.

name: SL PELVIC BRIDGE HIP THRUST (LOADED)
description: Level 5 unilateral strength. Adds load to the single-leg thrust, building independent hip extension capacity. High carryover to single-leg athletic activities including sprinting, cutting, and jumping. Progress load conservatively — compensatory lumbar extension is the primary error to monitor.

name: LONG LEVER HIP THRUST (BW & LOADED)
description: Level 7 advanced lever challenge. Extending the legs beyond the standard position dramatically increases the moment arm, making the bodyweight version as demanding as a moderately loaded standard thrust. High coordination demand — ensure athletes can maintain spinal neutral throughout.

name: LANDMINE HIP THRUSTERS
description: Level 8 guided arc strength. The fixed arc of the landmine provides partial stability while loading the hip thrust with a unique angle of resistance. Excellent for athletes who struggle with bar positioning on conventional BB thrusts or who need a guided transition to heavy bilateral hip extension.

name: BOX STEP UPS (BW)
description: Level 1 unilateral pattern. Stepping onto an elevated surface demands single-leg hip and knee extension in a controlled, low-velocity environment. Use to introduce unilateral loading mechanics before adding external resistance; assess pelvic control and trunk stability during the step.

name: LOADED STEP UPS (IPSI & CONTRA)
description: Level 3 load placement variation. Ipsilateral loading mimics a suitcase carry; contralateral loading shifts the center of mass away from the stepping leg, increasing demand on the hip abductors. Alternate between positions to develop complete frontal plane stability.

name: BB STEP UPS (FRONT RACK & BACK RACK)
description: Level 4 maximal bilateral load. Barbell loading increases systemic demand significantly. Front rack position forces thoracic extension and high anterior core bracing; back rack allows heavier loading with less postural complexity.

name: LANDMINE STEP UPS (FRONT RACK, IPSI & CONTRA)
description: Level 5 guided arc loading. The landmine constrains the bar path, reducing the stability demand of a free barbell while still achieving high loading. The arc of the bar encourages an upright torso and reinforces proper hip drive mechanics.

name: BW OVERHEAD STEP UPS (FRONT | LAT | ROT)
description: Level 6 multi-planar mobility challenge. Combining an overhead reach with the step exposes thoracic and shoulder mobility restrictions that don't appear in standard step-up patterns. Lateral and rotational reach variations add frontal and transverse plane demands.

name: LOADED OH STEP UPS (KB, DB, PLATE, BB, MB, SB)
description: Level 7 overhead stability under load. Progresses the overhead reach by adding resistance, increasing the demand on shoulder stability, thoracic extension, and anti-rotation core control simultaneously with single-leg strength.

name: ZERCHER HOLD STEP UPS (FORWARD & LAT)
description: Level 8 anterior core overload. The Zercher position loads the anterior chain maximally — the athlete must fight forward collapse with every step. Lateral variations add frontal plane challenge and higher hip abductor demand.

name: 3 POINT CONTACT STICK HIP HINGE
description: Level 1 motor learning drill. The stick against the spine (head, thoracic, sacrum) provides proprioceptive feedback to teach the athlete what a neutral spine hinge feels like in three dimensions. Non-negotiable foundation drill for any athlete who cannot disassociate hip flexion from lumbar flexion.

name: B/L DB BUM TO WALL HIP HINGE
description: Level 2 spatial awareness drill. The wall gives the athlete a target for the hips and a hard stop that prevents over-hinging or losing the hip crease. Builds the hip-back relationship before the athlete must manage an external load on the spine.

name: BANDED GOOD MORNINGS
description: Level 3 reactive pattern training. Band resistance accommodates to the movement — lighter at the bottom where the athlete is weakest, heavier at the top. Teaches the posterior chain to fire through the full range of extension and reinforces lockout mechanics.

name: LOADED GM (PLATE, MB, SB, KB, DB)
description: Level 4 anterior load progression. Holding implements in front of the body increases the moment arm and challenges the erectors and hamstrings under manageable load. Sandbag and stability ball variations introduce instability demands.

name: BB BACK RACK GM
description: Level 5 maximal posterior chain loading. Barbell on the back creates the highest spinal loading of the good morning family. Reserve for athletes who have demonstrated clean hinge mechanics under lighter loads; small technical errors become significant under heavy barbell.

name: LANDMINE GOOD MORNINGS
description: Level 6 guided spinal loading. The arc of the landmine reduces the risk of excessive forward lean and guides the athlete into a consistent movement pattern. Use as a transition between lighter loaded good mornings and heavy barbell variations.

name: ZERCHER HOLD GM (PLATE, BB)
description: Level 7 anti-flexion overload. Zercher carry dramatically increases anterior core demand, forcing the athlete to brace maximally to prevent spinal flexion during the hinge. Only appropriate for athletes with high baseline core strength and confirmed neutral hinge mechanics.

name: B/L KB SWINGS
description: Level 1 hip hinge power introduction. The two-handed swing teaches explosive hip extension under load with low coordination demand. The most important teaching point: power comes from hips snapping to extension, not from pulling with the arms. Use as the primary hinge power developer for beginners.

name: B/L KB DOUBLE LOADED SWINGS
description: Level 2 bilateral load increase. Two kettlebells increase systemic loading while maintaining bilateral symmetry. Demands higher lat engagement and thoracic stiffness to prevent the doubled load from pulling the torso into flexion.

name: B/L KB BREAK SWINGS
description: Level 3 deceleration control. The 'break' variation introduces intentional deceleration phases that require eccentric posterior chain control. Develops resilience for the hamstrings and reinforces the hinge loading position under fatigue.

name: SINGLE HAND KB SWINGS
description: Level 4 anti-rotation demand. Single-arm swings create a rotational torque that the obliques must counteract on every rep. A significant increase in trunk stability demand over bilateral variations; assess for lateral trunk shift or hip drop before progressing.

name: SINGLE HAND KB ALTERNATING SWINGS
description: Level 5 coordination and rhythm. Hand switches at the top of the swing add a coordination layer and require precise timing. Use in conditioning circuits — the alternating pattern maintains metabolic load while allowing brief neural recovery between hands.

name: HK SA KB SWINGS BETWEEN LEGS
description: Level 6 hip mobility and range extension. The half-kneeling single-arm between-legs swing maximizes hip flexion range at the bottom, demanding higher hamstring flexibility and hip mobility than standard swings. Exposes hip flexor tightness immediately.

name: SUITCASE KB SWINGS
description: Level 7 frontal plane power. Holding the kettlebell in a suitcase grip shifts the load laterally, adding hip abductor demand and anti-lateral-flexion challenge to the standard hinge power pattern.

name: DB RDL
description: Level 1 hinge strength introduction. Dumbbells allow for a natural hand path and require no barbell technique, making this the safest entry point for loaded RDL mechanics. Use to establish the hip-hinge loading position: soft knee, packed shoulders, spine neutral throughout the full range.

name: KB RDL
description: Level 2 grip and stability progression. The offset center of mass of the kettlebell requires more grip and forearm engagement than a dumbbell, adding a stability challenge without increasing the complexity of the movement pattern.

name: BB RDL
description: Level 3 maximal loading capacity. The barbell allows heavier loads and symmetric upper body position. Introduces the need for proper bar path management — the bar must stay in contact with or skim the thighs throughout the descent.

name: STAGGERED STANCE RDL
description: Level 4 unilateral bias. One foot slightly behind shifts 60–70% of the load to the front leg without fully removing the rear foot as a balance aid. Use as a regression from single-leg RDL for athletes who lack the balance or hip stability for a true unilateral pattern.

name: SINGLE LEG B/L LOADED RDL
description: Level 5 single-leg strength with bilateral load. Both hands hold load but only one leg is the primary driver. Increases the demand on the glute and hamstring of the stance leg while controlling pelvic rotation through the movement.

name: SINGLE LEG LOADED RDL (IPSI & CONTRA)
description: Level 6 unilateral strength with load variation. Ipsilateral load (same side as stance leg) challenges lateral hip stability; contralateral load shifts the center of mass away from the stance leg, increasing the hip abductor demand. Alternate to develop complete frontal plane control.

name: TANDEM STANCE SA KB RDL
description: Level 7 balance and coordination challenge. The tandem stance (one foot directly in front of the other) narrows the base of support significantly, requiring high proprioceptive demand and ankle stability in addition to standard RDL mechanics.

name: BAND ASSISTED DEAD LIFTS (KB, DB, BB, SB, MB)
description: Level 1 accommodating resistance regression. Band assistance deloads the bottom of the lift where the athlete is weakest, allowing practice of the full movement with a reduced effective load. Use for athletes who cannot yet maintain a neutral spine when initiating the pull from the floor.

name: SUMO DEAD LIFT (DB, KB, BB, PLATE, MB, SB)
description: Level 2 hip-width variation. The wide stance reduces the range of motion and allows the torso to remain more upright than conventional, biasing the adductors and inner hamstrings. Use for athletes with limited hip mobility in the conventional stance or long femur proportions.

name: TRAP BAR DEAD LIFT (B/L & STAGGERED)
description: Level 3 beginner-friendly max load. The trap bar places the load alongside the body rather than in front, reducing the moment arm on the lumbar spine and making it the safest path to heavy deadlift loading. Use as the primary strength builder for athletes who lack the mobility for a conventional pull.

name: STIFF LEG DEAD LIFT (KB, DB, BB)
description: Level 4 hamstring isolation. Minimal knee bend places the hamstrings on maximum stretch throughout the movement. High specificity for posterior chain hypertrophy; contraindicated for athletes with significant hamstring tightness until mobility is addressed.

name: CONVENTIONAL DEAD LIFT (KB, DB, BB)
description: Level 5 foundational strength. The classic bilateral pull from the floor. Demands full integration of hip hinge mechanics, lat engagement, and intra-abdominal pressure. The benchmark movement for total posterior chain output.

name: SINGLE LEG DEAD LIFT (KB, DB, BB)
description: Level 6 unilateral strength. Single-leg deadlift demands high hip stability, anti-rotation core control, and balance simultaneously with significant load. High transfer to sprinting, cutting, and landing mechanics.

name: TANDEM STANCE SA KB DL
description: Level 7 proprioceptive challenge. Narrow tandem base removes the typical stability of a shoulder-width stance, requiring the ankle, knee, and hip stabilizers to manage load in an unstable alignment. Use for advanced athletes seeking to bridge single-leg strength to sport-specific demands.

name: LANDMINE DEAD LIFTS (B/L & U/L)
description: Level 8 arc-guided pulling. The arc of the landmine guides the bar into the hips naturally, making it an excellent teaching tool for athletes who lose their bar path in conventional pulls. Unilateral landmine deadlifts add a rotation component and are high carry-over to rotational sport actions.

name: ASSISTED NORDICS (BAND, OF THE BENCH)
description: Level 1 eccentric introduction. Band or bench assistance reduces the loading of the hamstrings at the most vulnerable point of the movement — the lengthened position. Use to introduce Nordic mechanics without exceeding the athlete's current hamstring strength-to-bodyweight ratio.

name: NORDICS (BW)
description: Level 2 hamstring tendon resilience builder. Bodyweight Nordics are the gold-standard evidence-based exercise for reducing hamstring strain injury risk. The extreme eccentric load through full knee extension range builds tendon stiffness and proximal hamstring capacity.

name: LOADED NORDICS (MB, SB, PLATE, KB, DB, BB)
description: Level 3 maximal eccentric loading. External load increases the demand beyond bodyweight, extending the hamstring adaptation curve for advanced athletes. Requires significant eccentric strength — only progress here once the athlete can complete 5+ clean BW Nordic reps.

name: RAZOR CURLS (BW & LOADED)
description: Level 4 hip-flexion Nordic variation. The razor curl allows slight hip flexion throughout the movement, shifting emphasis slightly toward the proximal hamstring and changing the tendon angle. Use for athletes with distal hamstring tendinopathy or as a variation stimulus after long Nordic blocks.

name: BAND RESISTED OH PRESS (STANDING & SEATED)
description: Level 1 corrective drill. Elastic resistance increases tension toward lockout forcing continuous scapular upward rotation and trunk stiffness throughout the press. Use for athletes with poor overhead mechanics or FMS Shoulder Mobility limitations before progressing to external loading. Cue rib cage down and avoid lumbar extension during lockout.

name: BAND RESISTED OH PRESS (FROM BEHIND)
description: Level 2 activation drill. Band pull from posterior line biases scapular retraction and posterior cuff activation during the press pattern. Use for athletes who drift forward in overhead pressing or lose thoracic extension under load. Avoid excessive cervical extension during the press path.

name: BAND RESISTED SA OH PRESS (STANDING & SEATED)
description: Level 3 unilateral stability drill. Single-arm loading introduces anti-rotation demand forcing the trunk and pelvis to stabilize against asymmetrical tension. Use for athletes with left-right pressing asymmetries or poor frontal plane control.

name: BAND RESISTED SA OH PRESS (FROM BEHIND)
description: Level 4 anti-rotation progression. Posterior band resistance amplifies scapular stability demands while the unilateral pattern challenges rotational control. Use during return-to-press phases following shoulder instability or scapular dyskinesis.

name: PIKE PUSH UPS (B/L & U/L)
description: Level 5 bodyweight overhead progression. Elevating the hips vertically shifts loading toward the shoulders while reducing lower body contribution. Use for athletes transitioning from horizontal pressing toward vertical pressing patterns without external load. Maintain cervical neutrality and full scapular upward rotation.

name: HAND STAND PUSH UPS
description: Level 6 advanced bodyweight strength. Inverted pressing dramatically increases axial loading and demands full-body tension under unstable conditions. Use only for athletes with FMS Score 3 overhead competency and strong scapulothoracic control. Contraindicated for athletes lacking cervical stability or overhead mobility.

name: BB MILITARY PRESS
description: Level 7 foundational maximal strength. Strict bilateral barbell pressing removes lower body assistance forcing vertical force production through the trunk and shoulders. Use for athletes who demonstrate stable rib positioning and controlled scapular mechanics under load.

name: DOUBLE BB JAVELIN PRESS
description: Level 8 asymmetrical stability progression. Offset barbell loading creates rotational instability forcing extreme anti-rotation and shoulder packing. Use for advanced athletes preparing for contact sport or overhead power demands.

name: BB BACK PRESS
description: Level 9 advanced mobility-strength drill. Pressing from behind the neck requires high thoracic extension and shoulder external rotation under load. Use only for athletes with elite overhead mobility and no history of shoulder impingement. Contraindicated for athletes with anterior shoulder instability.

name: SEATED OH BB PRESS (BOX TO FREE WEIGHT)
description: Level 1 supported regression. The seated position removes lower body contribution allowing isolation of scapular upward rotation and pressing mechanics. Use for athletes who compensate with lumbar extension during standing presses.

name: TK & HH OH BB PRESS
description: Level 2 trunk integration drill. Tall kneeling and half kneeling positions reduce compensation from the hips while increasing pelvic and core stabilization demands. Use for athletes who cannot maintain stacked posture during vertical pressing.

name: BB STRICT PRESS
description: Level 3 foundational press pattern. Eliminating leg drive forces force transfer entirely through trunk stiffness and shoulder mechanics. Use during foundational strength phases before introducing ballistic overhead work.

name: BB STRICT PRESS
description: Level 4 loaded strength progression. Increased loading challenges scapular control and thoracic extension without assistance from lower body momentum. Use for athletes progressing toward maximal vertical force production.

name: BB BACK RACKED OH PRESS
description: Level 5 mobility-intensive strength progression. Back rack position increases shoulder external rotation and thoracic extension demands throughout the press. Use only after demonstrating clean front-rack and strict press competency.

name: BB MILITARY PRESS
description: Level 6 maximal bilateral strength. Upright stance and strict pressing mechanics maximize axial loading through the kinetic chain. Use for advanced athletes developing foundational overhead strength qualities.

name: BB MILITARY PRESS
description: Level 7 maximal force progression. Heavy bilateral overhead pressing develops high-threshold motor unit recruitment and full-body rigidity. Use during maximal strength phases for collision and overhead athletes.

name: SEATED OH DB PRESS (BOX TO FREE WEIGHT)
description: Level 1 independent stability drill. Dumbbells allow natural shoulder movement while the seated position minimizes balance constraints. Use for athletes with asymmetrical pressing mechanics or limited barbell overhead tolerance.

name: TK & HK OH DB PRESS
description: Level 2 anti-extension progression. Kneeling variations restrict compensatory lumbar movement while increasing core engagement. Use for athletes who arch excessively during standing overhead work.

name: ALTERNATING OH DB PRESS
description: Level 3 dynamic stability drill. Alternating arm action creates rhythmic anti-rotation demand forcing trunk stabilization between repetitions. Use for athletes lacking unilateral overhead coordination.

name: ALTERNATING OH DB PRESS
description: Level 4 unilateral loading progression. Independent loading magnifies asymmetry exposure and scapular control requirements. Use during structural balance phases in overhead athletes.

name: CUBAN PRESS
description: Level 5 rotator cuff integration drill. Combines external rotation with pressing to reinforce scapular positioning and cuff activation. Use during shoulder resiliency phases or post-rehabilitation overhead progression. Avoid excessive loading; quality of movement governs progression.

name: ALTERNATING OH DB PRESS
description: Level 6 advanced unilateral strength. Continuous anti-rotation demand under higher loads challenges trunk stiffness and shoulder sequencing. Use for athletes transitioning toward unilateral overhead power work.

name: SEATED OH KB PRESS (BOX TO FREE WEIGHT)

name: TK & HK FROM THE BOX OH DB PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: TK & HK INVERTED KB OH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 4 advanced stability progression. Bottom-up kettlebell position magnifies instability forcing maximal grip, cuff, and trunk activation. Use for athletes with adequate baseline overhead competency but poor force transfer.

name: ALTERNATING OH KB PRESS
description: Level 5 unilateral overhead coordination drill. Alternating kettlebell mechanics challenge timing, anti-rotation control, and scapular sequencing. Use during transitional phases toward ballistic overhead work.

name: INVERTED KB PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 6 high-threshold stability drill. Bottom-up loading punishes poor wrist alignment and scapular instability instantly. Use only for athletes with strong grip integrity and clean overhead mechanics.

name: TK STRICT PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: HK PUSH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: HK STRICT PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: STANDING PUSH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: STANDING STRICT PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)

name: SEATED OH SM PRESS

name: TK & HK OH SM PRESS

name: STRICT PRESS SM (BACK & FRONT RACK)

name: TK & HK OH PRESS

name: STANDING OH PRESS

name: B/L JAVELIN OH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 3 anti-rotation overhead progression. Long lever loading magnifies shoulder stabilization and rotational control demands. Use for athletes preparing for throwing or striking mechanics.

name: CHAOS BAR OH PRESS (STICKY BB)
description: Level 4 reactive stability drill. Suspended loading introduces oscillation forcing reflexive cuff activation and scapular timing corrections. Use during late-stage rehabilitation or advanced stabilization phases.

name: BB ACCOMMODATING CHAINS OH PRESS
description: Level 5 dynamic resistance progression. Chain loading alters resistance through the ROM requiring aggressive acceleration into lockout. Use for advanced strength-power development blocks.

name: DOUBLE HANGING PLATES OH PRESS
description: Level 6 perturbation stability progression. Independently moving plates create continuous instability demanding full kinetic-chain stiffness. Use only for athletes with advanced overhead competency and trunk control.

name: PIZZA PLATE OH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 7 long-lever instability drill. Plate positioning away from the centerline magnifies shoulder moment arms and anti-rotation requirements. Use for overhead athletes needing refined scapular stability.

name: BOTTOMS UP PLATE OH PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 8 advanced reflexive stability drill. Unstable loading punishes poor hand positioning and scapular control instantly. Use during high-level proprioceptive and shoulder resilience phases.

name: BENCH KNEELING OH PRESS (DB, KB, JAVELIN, PLATE)
description: Level 9 integrated instability progression. Elevated kneeling posture combines balance disruption with complex overhead loading strategies. Use for elite athletes requiring full-body stabilization under overhead perturbation.

name: TRAP BAR Z PRESS
description: Level 1 supported overhead stability drill. Sitting on the floor removes lower body contribution while the neutral trap bar grip reduces shoulder external rotation stress during pressing. Use for athletes with limited thoracic extension or poor standing overhead mechanics who still require vertical pressing exposure. Cue full trunk stiffness and avoid lumbar collapse at lockout.

name: INVERTED KB OH Z PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 2 reflexive stability progression. Bottom-up kettlebell loading magnifies wrist, rotator cuff, and scapular stabilization demands while the seated posture eliminates leg-driven compensation. Use for athletes with unstable overhead patterns or poor shoulder centration during pressing. Terminate the set immediately if kettlebell alignment becomes unstable.

name: PIZZA PLATE Z PRESS
description: Level 3 long-lever shoulder stability drill. Wide plate positioning increases moment arm demands forcing continuous scapular control and anti-wobble stabilization. Use for athletes who display excessive humeral drift or weak lockout mechanics in vertical pressing.

name: FOAM ROLLER Z PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 4 unstable posture integration drill. Sitting on the foam roller increases pelvic instability forcing the trunk to maintain alignment while pressing overhead. Use for athletes who lose midline control or rib positioning during seated presses. Cue stacked ribs and pelvis throughout the movement.

name: LANDMINE Z PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 5 angled pressing progression. The landmine arc reduces pure vertical shoulder stress while still demanding trunk stiffness and scapular upward rotation from the seated position. Use for athletes returning from overhead irritation or those lacking full shoulder flexion capacity.

name: REVERSE LANDMINE Z PRESS (DOUBLE & SA)
description: Level 6 posterior-chain integrated press. Reversed landmine loading shifts resistance behind the centerline increasing thoracic extension and posterior shoulder stabilization demands. Use for athletes who collapse forward during overhead pressing or lack scapular retraction strength.

name: LEG RAISED Z PRESS ON THE BENCH
description: Level 7 advanced trunk stiffness progression. Elevating the legs removes additional base-of-support stability forcing maximal anterior core engagement during the overhead press. Use for athletes who compensate with hip flexor dominance or excessive lumbar extension under load.

name: BENT LEG Z PRESS
description: Level 8 foundational Z press progression. Bent knee positioning reduces hamstring tension allowing athletes to maintain a more upright pelvis and thoracic posture during seated pressing. Use for athletes introducing the Z press pattern before progressing to straight-leg or unstable variations.

name: DEAD HANG SCAP RETRACTIONS
description: Level 1 corrective drill. Hanging position teaches scapular depression and upward rotation control without elbow flexion compensation. Use for athletes with poor scapular awareness or FMS Shoulder Mobility limitations.

name: BAND ASSISTED SCAP PULLS
description: Level 2 assisted activation drill. Band unloading reduces bodyweight demand allowing athletes to isolate scapular movement mechanics. Use for athletes unable to control active hanging positions independently.

name: ACTIVE HANGS
description: Level 3 foundational stability drill. Maintaining active shoulder positioning under full bodyweight develops shoulder centration and grip endurance. Use during early hanging competency phases.

name: SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 4 scapular strength progression. Controlled vertical displacement without elbow bend reinforces lower trap and lat engagement. Use for athletes who initiate pull ups with excessive arm dominance.

name: TEMPO SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 5 motor control progression. Slower eccentric and concentric phases increase time under tension and positional awareness. Use for athletes lacking scapular rhythm or stability endurance.

name: WEIGHTED SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 6 loaded scapular strength drill. External load magnifies lower trap and lat recruitment under hanging conditions. Use for advanced athletes progressing toward maximal vertical pulling strength.

name: SINGLE ARM SCAP HOLDS
description: Level 7 unilateral stability drill. Single-arm hanging dramatically increases anti-rotation and scapular stabilization demand. Use for athletes progressing toward unilateral pulling competency.

name: OFFSET SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 8 asymmetrical loading progression. Uneven grip positions create rotational instability forcing reflexive trunk stabilization. Use for climbers and combat athletes requiring asymmetrical pulling resilience.

name: RING SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 9 unstable surface progression. Rings introduce multidirectional instability demanding constant scapular correction. Use only for athletes with advanced hanging competency.

name: EXPLOSIVE SCAP PULL UPS
description: Level 10 reactive pulling drill. Rapid scapular depression and elevation trains elastic lat function and explosive initiation mechanics. Use during advanced power and gymnastics preparation phases.

name: BAND ASSISTED PULL UPS
description: Level 1 assisted regression. Elastic assistance reduces effective bodyweight allowing the athlete to maintain scapular depression and vertical pulling mechanics through full ROM. Use for athletes with FMS Score 1–2 upper body pulling competency or insufficient concentric pulling strength. Cue ribs down and avoid excessive kipping through the lower body.

name: FEET SUPPORTED PULL UPS
description: Level 2 supported patterning drill. Lower body contact decreases loading demand while preserving full vertical pull sequencing and grip mechanics. Use for athletes who lose scapular positioning or cannot control the eccentric phase independently.

name: TRX ASSISTED PULL UPS
description: Level 3 motor control progression. Suspension assistance permits adjustable unloading while increasing scapular stabilization demand through free-moving handles. Use for athletes with asymmetrical pulling patterns or poor shoulder centration during hanging movements.

name: ECCENTRIC PULL UPS
description: Level 4 eccentric overload drill. Controlled lowering increases tendon stiffness and eccentric lat strength without requiring full concentric capability. Use during foundational pull-up development or return-to-pull phases after upper limb injury. Maintain a strict 3–5 second eccentric tempo.

name: ISO HOLD PULL UPS
description: Level 5 positional stability drill. Isometric holds reinforce scapular depression and trunk stiffness at mechanically weak pull-up positions. Use for athletes who fail at transition points or lose upper back tension near the top range.

name: PARTNER ASSISTED PULL UPS
description: Level 6 adaptive assistance progression. External assistance can be adjusted in real time to maintain movement quality under fatigue. Use during high-volume accumulation phases where strict pulling mechanics must remain intact.

name: CHAOS BAND PULL UPS
description: Level 7 reactive stability drill. Oscillating band tension creates unpredictable perturbations forcing reflexive scapular and trunk stabilization. Use for advanced athletes requiring reactive shoulder control for contact or grappling sports.

name: OFFSET GRIP PULL UPS
description: Level 8 asymmetrical loading progression. Uneven hand positions increase unilateral pulling demand and anti-rotation trunk control. Use for climbers, wrestlers, and athletes displaying dominant-side pulling strategies.

name: RING ASSISTED PULL UPS
description: Level 9 unstable vertical pull progression. Rings increase shoulder stabilization and grip demand throughout the pull path. Use only for athletes with competent fixed-bar pull-up mechanics and stable scapular control.

name: LIGHT LOADED PULL UPS

name: NEUTRAL GRIP LAT PULL DOWN

description: Level 5 asymmetrical loading drill. Offset load biases one side of the trunk and challenges anti-lateral flexion during rotation. Use for athletes with side-to-side trunk control deficits or asymmetrical sport demands.

name: KB ROTATIONAL PRESS
description: Level 6 integrated strength drill. The press links hip rotation, trunk transfer, and upper-body force production with kettlebell load. Use for athletes progressing from isolated rotation into loaded total-body patterns.

name: SA KB WINDMILL
description: Level 7 advanced mobility-strength drill. Single-arm overhead loading demands thoracic rotation, hip hinge control, and shoulder stability. Use only for athletes with adequate overhead mobility and clean hinge mechanics.

name: LOADED KB WINDMILL
description: Level 8 advanced loaded mobility drill. Added load increases the demand on obliques, QL, shoulder stability, and hip control through a rotational hinge. Use for advanced athletes with no lumbar symptoms and strong overhead position control.

name: LANDMINE ANTI-ROTATION HOLD
description: Level 1 loaded stability drill. The angled bar creates rotational torque while the athlete maintains square hips and ribs. Use for athletes who need a joint-friendly loaded anti-rotation option.

name: LANDMINE ROTATIONS
description: Level 2 controlled rotation drill. The landmine arc guides the path and reduces degrees of freedom during torso rotation. Use for athletes learning loaded rotation before free-weight or high-speed patterns.

name: HALF KNEELING LANDMINE ROTATIONS
description: Level 3 kneeling rotation progression. Half kneeling restricts pelvic compensation while the landmine loads a fixed rotational arc. Use for athletes who rotate cleanly on the floor but lose control when load is added.

name: LANDMINE 180s
description: Level 4 dynamic rotation drill. Moving the bar across a wide arc trains controlled trunk rotation and deceleration side to side. Use for athletes who need repeatable rotational strength without full ballistic throwing.

name: LANDMINE RAINBOWS
description: Level 5 strength-control drill. The bar path crosses overhead and across midline, challenging trunk control through a long lever. Use for athletes who need anti-extension and anti-rotation control in diagonal patterns.

name: LANDMINE ROTATIONAL PRESS
description: Level 6 integrated press drill. The angled press links lower-body drive, trunk rotation, and upper-body force through a guided bar path. Use for athletes preparing for rotational pushing, striking, or throwing mechanics.

name: LANDMINE SHOT PUT
description: Level 7 power drill. The movement converts hip rotation into an explosive angled press with heavier loading than a medicine ball. Use for advanced athletes in strength-power phases who can maintain rib and pelvis alignment.

name: EXPLOSIVE LANDMINE ROTATIONS
description: Level 8 advanced power drill. The landmine loads fast transverse-plane acceleration and controlled braking at end range. Use for trained athletes who already own slower landmine rotations and need high-output rotational work.

name: DB TORSO TWISTS
description: Level 1 loaded rotation drill. The dumbbell provides simple external resistance while the athlete controls torso rotation through a manageable range. Use for athletes beginning loaded rotation after bodyweight patterning.

name: DB OFFSET HOLDS
description: Level 2 anti-rotation stability drill. Uneven dumbbell loading creates asymmetrical trunk demand without requiring visible rotation. Use for athletes with lateral trunk shift, poor bracing, or early loaded core needs.

name: DB ROTATIONAL PRESS
description: Level 3 integrated press drill. The dumbbell links hip turn, trunk rotation, and pressing action with moderate load. Use for athletes who need coordinated rotational pressing before faster power work.

name: DB WOODCHOPS
description: Level 4 diagonal strength drill. The dumbbell trains high-to-low or cross-body rotation without external cable guidance. Use for athletes who need free-weight control through diagonal trunk patterns.

name: DB HIGH TO LOW CHOPS
description: Level 5 diagonal control drill. The high-to-low path emphasizes downward rotational strength and trunk braking. Use for athletes who need stronger control during cutting, striking, or downward throwing actions.

name: DB LOW TO HIGH CHOPS
description: Level 6 diagonal control drill. The low-to-high path trains upward rotational force while resisting lumbar extension. Use for athletes who overarch during lifts, serves, or rising rotational actions.

name: DB ROTATIONAL THRUSTERS
description: Level 7 total-body power drill. The movement combines squat drive, trunk rotation, and overhead pressing into one coordinated pattern. Use for advanced athletes who maintain alignment under fatigue and multi-joint loading.

name: DB ROTATIONAL SNATCHES
description: Level 8 advanced power drill. The dumbbell snatch adds rapid hip extension and rotation with overhead catch stability. Use for advanced athletes with strong hinge mechanics, shoulder control, and no lumbar irritation.

name: BB OFFSET HOLDS
description: Level 1 loaded stability drill. The offset barbell position creates a strong anti-rotation and anti-lateral flexion demand. Use for athletes needing trunk stiffness under load before dynamic barbell rotation.

name: BB LANDMINE TWISTS
description: Level 2 guided rotation drill. The barbell landmine arc constrains the path and reduces technical complexity. Use for athletes learning loaded rotation with a stable and predictable implement.

name: BB ROTATIONAL PRESS
description: Level 3 strength integration drill. The barbell pattern links lower-body rotation and pressing force through a controlled line of drive. Use for athletes who need rotational strength before explosive press variations.

name: BB ZERCHER ROTATIONS
description: Level 4 anterior-load rotation drill. The Zercher position loads the anterior trunk and forces upright posture during rotation. Use for athletes who collapse forward or lose rib position under rotational load.

name: BB OFFSET WALKING ROTATIONS
description: Level 5 locomotion stability drill. Offset barbell loading combines gait, trunk stiffness, and controlled rotation under asymmetrical demand. Use for athletes who need trunk control while moving rather than standing still.

name: BB JAVELIN ROTATIONS
description: Level 6 unilateral bar control drill. The javelin position challenges shoulder stability and trunk rotation with a long, unstable lever. Use for advanced athletes with strong overhead control and asymmetrical sport demands.

name: BB ROTATIONAL PUSH PRESS
description: Level 7 power-strength drill. The push press uses leg drive and trunk rotation to move heavier load explosively. Use for trained athletes in power phases who can brace and rotate without lumbar extension.

name: BB ROTATIONAL CLEAN
description: Level 8 advanced power drill. The clean integrates rotational hip drive, trunk stiffness, and rapid bar turnover. Use only for advanced athletes with strong Olympic-lift competency and clean transverse-plane mechanics.

name: BEAR CRAWL REACHES
description: Level 1 crawling corrective drill. The bear position trains trunk anti-rotation while one hand reaches away from the base of support. Use for athletes with poor trunk stability, shoulder control deficits, or FMS rotary stability limitations.

name: DEADCUG ROTATIONS
description: Level 2 supine motor-control drill. Supine position reduces balance demand while limb motion challenges trunk control against rotation. Use for athletes who cannot maintain rib-pelvis position during basic core patterns.

name: BIRD DOG ROTATIONS
description: Level 3 rotary stability drill. Contralateral support challenges the trunk to control rotation while the limbs move. Use for athletes with FMS rotary stability deficits or poor lumbopelvic control.

name: CRAWLING ROTATIONS
description: Level 4 locomotor control drill. Crawling adds reciprocal limb movement while the trunk resists and produces controlled rotation. Use for athletes progressing from static rotary stability into coordinated ground-based movement.

name: SPRINTER BAND ROTATIONS
description: Level 5 acceleration-pattern drill. Band resistance links trunk rotation with sprinter posture and contralateral limb drive. Use for field athletes who need rotation control during acceleration mechanics.

name: SINGLE LEG ROTATIONAL REACHES
description: Level 6 single-leg control drill. Reaching across the body challenges hip stability, foot pressure, and trunk rotation simultaneously. Use for athletes who lose knee or pelvis control during cutting and landing patterns.

name: ROTATIONAL BOUND TO STICK
description: Level 7 plyometric control drill. The bound creates rotational momentum and the stick phase trains deceleration and landing control. Use in return-to-sport phases for athletes who need transverse-plane landing stability.

name: ROTATIONAL HOP TO THROW
description: Level 8 advanced transfer drill. The hop adds elastic lower-body loading before the athlete transfers force into a rotational throw. Use for advanced field and court athletes in late power or sport-prep phases.

name: MB REACTIVE CATCH ROTATIONS
description: Level 1 reactive control drill. The catch introduces external timing and low-level rotational perturbation. Use for athletes who need trunk stiffness under unpredictable input before producing force.

name: MB STEP BEHIND THROWS
description: Level 2 sequencing drill. The step-behind pattern teaches lower-body momentum transfer into rotational medicine ball release. Use for athletes who arm-throw or fail to use hip rotation during power work.

name: MB SHUFFLE THROWS
description: Level 3 dynamic power drill. The shuffle adds lateral movement before rotation, increasing timing and footwork demand. Use for court and field athletes who need to produce rotation after repositioning.

name: MB OPEN STANCE THROWS
description: Level 4 power expression drill. Open stance increases hip availability and teaches aggressive trunk rotation from a wider base. Use when athletes need higher-output throwing without complex footwork.

name: MB CLOSED STANCE THROWS
