name: TALL CLEAN PULLS
description: Level 1 Olympic derivative drill. The tall start removes the dip and teaches vertical pull timing from extension. Use for athletes learning clean mechanics before adding hinge or floor positions.

name: CLEAN PULLS
description: Level 2 pull-strength drill. The clean pull trains coordinated extension through ankles, knees, and hips without the catch. Use for athletes who need power development but are not ready to receive the bar.

name: MID THIGH CLEAN PULLS
description: Level 3 position-specific pull drill. The mid-thigh start emphasizes the power position and reduces complexity from the floor. Use for athletes who miss extension timing or pull early with the arms.

name: HANG HIGH PULLS
description: Level 4 explosive pull drill. The hang position adds hip loading while the high pull teaches upward force transfer after extension. Use for athletes progressing from pulls toward clean derivatives.

name: HANG POWER CLEANS
description: Level 5 receiving drill. The hang start limits setup complexity while training explosive extension into a partial catch. Use for athletes with adequate front-rack mobility and stable landing posture.

name: POWER CLEANS
description: Level 6 Olympic power drill. Pulling from the floor integrates setup, extension, turnover, and catch timing. Use for trained athletes with clean hinge, front-rack, and coaching supervision.

name: POWER SNATCHES
description: Level 7 advanced Olympic drill. The snatch requires rapid extension and overhead receiving with high shoulder and trunk demand. Use only for athletes with strong overhead mobility and stable Olympic-lift mechanics.

name: CONTRAST OLYMPIC COMPLEX
description: Level 8 advanced contrast complex. Olympic derivatives paired with jumps or throws use high neural drive to potentiate power output. Use in performance phases for technically competent lifters with no current pain flags.

name: WALL DRIVES
description: Level 1 acceleration-position drill. Wall support fixes torso angle and teaches forceful ground projection through the stance leg. Use for athletes who pop upright early or overstride during acceleration.

name: A-MARCHES
description: Level 2 sprint-mechanics drill. The march isolates posture, front-side knee drive, and dorsiflexed foot position at low speed. Use for athletes cleaning up sprint mechanics before elastic drills.

name: A-SKIPS
description: Level 3 elastic sprint drill. The skip adds rhythm and bounce to the A-march pattern while preserving posture. Use when athletes can march cleanly but lack stiffness and timing.

name: DRIBBLE RUNS
description: Level 4 rhythm-speed drill. Low-amplitude contacts train turnover, stiffness, and front-side mechanics under faster rhythm. Use for athletes who overstride or strike too far in front during sprint buildups.

name: RESISTED ACCELERATIONS
description: Level 5 resisted sprint drill. External resistance increases horizontal force demand while controlling speed. Use for athletes who need better projection and lower-body drive out of the start.

name: SLED SPRINTS
description: Level 6 loaded acceleration drill. The sled provides measurable horizontal load while the athlete maintains acceleration posture. Use in power phases for athletes with stable sprint mechanics and adequate hamstring tolerance.

name: ASSISTED SPRINTS
description: Level 7 overspeed drill. Assistance increases step frequency and challenges the athlete to maintain mechanics above normal speed. Use only for advanced sprinters with clean mechanics and no hamstring risk signs.

name: REACTIVE ACCELERATIONS
description: Level 8 reactive acceleration drill. External cues train start response, projection, and reacceleration under decision pressure. Use in late performance phases for athletes who already own planned acceleration work.

name: LINE HOPS
description: Level 1 reactive footwork drill. Small hops over a line train low-amplitude stiffness and foot placement accuracy. Use for athletes reintroducing plyometric contacts after landing mechanics are stable.

name: FAST FEET DRILLS
description: Level 2 rhythm and stiffness drill. Rapid low-level contacts train coordination, ankle stiffness, and posture without large jumps. Use for athletes who need foot speed before higher-force reactive drills.

name: POGO SERIES
description: Level 3 elastic contact drill. Repeated pogo variations train short ground-contact time and lower-leg stiffness. Use for athletes preparing the foot-ankle complex for jumping and sprinting.

name: REACTIVE POGOS
description: Level 4 reactive stiffness drill. Cue-driven changes in height, rhythm, or direction challenge elastic control. Use for athletes who can pogo cleanly and need adaptable foot mechanics.

name: DEPTH REBOUNDS
description: Level 5 reactive-strength drill. Dropping into an immediate rebound increases eccentric loading and shortens coupling time. Use for athletes with strong landing mechanics and adequate tendon readiness.

name: HURDLE REBOUNDS
description: Level 6 repeated reactive drill. Hurdles constrain rebound height and rhythm while maintaining fast contacts. Use for athletes who need reactive stiffness across repeated contacts.

name: MULTI-DIRECTIONAL REACTIVE HOPS
description: Level 7 multi-planar reactive drill. Directional changes challenge foot placement, braking, and elastic re-acceleration. Use for field and court athletes in late plyometric preparation.

name: CHAOS REACTIVE SERIES
description: Level 8 advanced reactive complex. Unpredictable cues, spacing, or contacts challenge perception, stiffness, and landing control together. Use for advanced athletes preparing for competition-speed plyometric demands.

name: MARCHING BOUNDS
description: Level 1 bounding preparation drill. Marching rhythm teaches arm-leg coordination and projection mechanics at low intensity. Use for athletes learning bound sequencing before flight time increases.

name: SKIP FOR DISTANCE
description: Level 2 horizontal rhythm drill. Skipping for distance trains projection while keeping contacts more controlled than full bounds. Use for athletes who need horizontal force expression with manageable landing demand.

name: POWER SKIPS
description: Level 3 vertical-horizontal power drill. Higher amplitude skips train coordinated arm drive, stiffness, and projection. Use for athletes who can skip rhythmically and need more power output.

name: ALTERNATING BOUNDS
description: Level 4 foundational bounding drill. Alternating contacts train horizontal projection, posture, and single-leg stiffness. Use for athletes moving from skips into true bounding mechanics.

name: CONTINUOUS BOUNDS
description: Level 5 repeated bounding drill. Consecutive bounds reduce reset time and train elastic force transfer across strides. Use for athletes with clean alternating bounds who need higher plyometric density.

name: SINGLE LEG BOUNDS
description: Level 6 unilateral bounding drill. Repeated same-leg contacts increase stiffness, hip control, and tendon demand. Use only after single-leg hop and landing mechanics are stable.

name: REACTIVE BOUNDS
description: Level 7 reactive bounding drill. External cues alter direction or timing and force rapid reorganization of bounding mechanics. Use for late-stage field athletes who need power under decision pressure.

name: MAX VELOCITY BOUNDS
description: Level 8 advanced speed-power drill. High-speed bounds emphasize front-side mechanics, stiffness, and horizontal force at near sprint rhythm. Use for advanced sprint athletes with mature mechanics and no hamstring warning signs.

name: VERTICAL JUMP COMPLEX
description: Level 1 performance power complex. Sequenced vertical jumps expose takeoff mechanics, landing control, and repeated power output. Use in power blocks for athletes who already pass basic landing screens.

name: BROAD JUMP COMPLEX
description: Level 2 horizontal power complex. Multiple broad-jump variations train projection, braking, and repeated horizontal force. Use for acceleration-focused athletes with clean broad jump landings.

name: HURDLE COMPLEX
description: Level 3 elastic hurdle complex. Hurdle sequences constrain rhythm, contact timing, and reactive stiffness. Use for athletes who need repeated elastic contacts after basic hurdle hops are stable.

name: DEPTH JUMP COMPLEX
description: Level 4 reactive-strength complex. Depth variations train eccentric absorption, short coupling time, and rebound power. Use only when depth drops and standard depth jumps are technically sound.

name: OLYMPIC COMPLEX
description: Level 5 barbell power complex. Olympic derivatives combine high-force pulls, catches, and explosive extensions. Use for technically competent lifters in structured power phases.

name: CONTRAST TRAINING
description: Level 6 strength-power contrast method. Heavy strength work paired with explosive movement uses potentiation to increase neural output. Use for trained athletes with adequate strength base and reliable landing mechanics.

name: FRENCH CONTRAST METHOD
description: Level 7 advanced contrast method. The sequence layers heavy, plyometric, loaded jump, and assisted explosive work to target multiple points on the force-velocity curve. Use for advanced athletes in short power blocks with close fatigue monitoring.

name: SPORT SPECIFIC POWER COMPLEX
description: Level 8 transfer power complex. Exercise selection matches sport stance, vector, rhythm, and decision demand to bridge training output into competition actions. Use in late preparation phases after general power qualities are established.

name: WALL DRIVES
description: Level 1 acceleration-position drill. The wall fixes torso angle and teaches forceful ground projection through the stance leg. Use for athletes who pop upright early, overstride, or cannot hold acceleration posture.

name: WALL SWITCHES
description: Level 2 acceleration-switch drill. Alternating switches train rapid hip exchange while the wall constrains trunk angle and shin position. Use for athletes who can hold wall-drive posture but lose rhythm during limb cycling.

name: A-MARCHES
description: Level 3 sprint-mechanics drill. The march isolates front-side knee drive, dorsiflexed foot position, and upright posture at low speed. Use for athletes with poor sprint rhythm or FMS asymmetry before elastic drills.

name: A-SKIPS
description: Level 4 elastic sprint drill. Skipping adds bounce and timing to the A-march pattern while preserving front-side mechanics. Use for athletes who march cleanly but lack stiffness and rhythm.

name: DRIBBLE RUNS
description: Level 5 rhythm-speed drill. Low-amplitude contacts train turnover, foot strike timing, and front-side mechanics under faster rhythm. Use for athletes who overstride or strike too far in front during sprint buildups.

name: RESISTED ACCELERATIONS
description: Level 6 resisted sprint drill. External resistance increases horizontal force demand while controlling sprint speed. Use for athletes who need stronger projection and cleaner body angle out of the start.

name: SLED SPRINTS
description: Level 7 loaded acceleration drill. The sled provides measurable horizontal load while the athlete maintains acceleration posture and step rhythm. Use in power phases for athletes with stable sprint mechanics and adequate hamstring tolerance.

name: ASSISTED ACCELERATIONS
description: Level 8 overspeed acceleration drill. Assistance increases step frequency and challenges the athlete to maintain mechanics beyond normal acceleration speed. Use only for advanced athletes with clean acceleration mechanics and no hamstring risk signs.

name: SNAP DOWNS
description: Level 1 deceleration-position drill. The rapid drop teaches the athlete to organize ankles, knees, hips, and trunk into a braking position. Use for FMS Score 1–2 athletes who land tall, noisy, or with valgus collapse.

name: DROP TO STICK
description: Level 2 landing-control drill. A small drop adds gravity-driven loading while the athlete freezes the landing position. Use for athletes who can snap down but lose alignment when impact is introduced.

name: FORWARD DECELERATION STICKS
description: Level 3 forward braking drill. Forward momentum adds horizontal braking demand while the stick phase removes rebound. Use for athletes who overrun stops or let the knee drift forward without hip control.

name: BACKWARD DECELERATION STICKS
description: Level 4 reverse braking drill. Backward movement challenges posterior foot placement and trunk control during stopping. Use for athletes who backpedal upright or stumble when retreating.

name: LATERAL DECELERATION STICKS
description: Level 5 lateral braking drill. Side-to-side momentum loads the hip abductors and trunk while the athlete sticks the stop. Use for athletes who collapse at the knee or trunk during shuffles and cuts.

name: MULTI-DIRECTIONAL STICKS
description: Level 6 multi-planar deceleration drill. Changing approach angles exposes braking control across sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes. Use for field and court athletes who stop well in one direction but fail under angle changes.

name: REACTIVE DECELERATIONS
description: Level 7 reactive braking drill. External cues delay the stop decision and force rapid foot placement and trunk organization. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned decelerations are stable.

name: CHAOS DECELERATIONS
description: Level 8 advanced deceleration drill. Unpredictable cues, approach speeds, or perturbations challenge braking mechanics under open-skill conditions. Use for advanced athletes preparing for competition-speed stopping demands.

name: MARCH RUNS
description: Level 1 linear-speed patterning drill. March-to-run rhythm bridges technical drills into low-speed running without maximal intensity. Use for athletes who need posture and limb timing before faster sprint work.

name: SKIP RUNS
description: Level 2 rhythm-speed drill. Skipping into running preserves elastic timing while gradually increasing stride frequency. Use for athletes who can march well but lose coordination when speed rises.

name: BUILD-UP RUNS
description: Level 3 acceleration-to-speed drill. Gradual speed increase lets the athlete organize posture, contact timing, and relaxation before maximal sprinting. Use for athletes returning to sprint exposure or cleaning up mechanics.

name: FLYING 10s
description: Level 4 max-velocity exposure drill. A build-in zone removes start mechanics and isolates 10 meters of upright sprint speed. Use for athletes ready for controlled high-speed exposure with limited volume.

name: FLYING 20s
description: Level 5 max-velocity capacity drill. The longer fly zone increases exposure time to upright sprint mechanics and elastic stiffness. Use for athletes who tolerate flying 10s and need more high-speed rhythm.

name: RESISTED SPRINTS
description: Level 6 resisted speed drill. External load increases projection demand while the athlete preserves stride mechanics. Use for athletes who need horizontal force development without sacrificing sprint shape.

name: ASSISTED SPRINTS
description: Level 7 overspeed drill. Assistance raises step frequency and challenges mechanics above normal top speed. Use only for advanced athletes with stable max-velocity mechanics and no hamstring warning signs.

name: CONTRAST SPEED RUNS
description: Level 8 contrast speed drill. Resisted or loaded runs paired with fast sprints use potentiation to raise neural output. Use in performance phases for trained athletes with mature sprint mechanics.

name: LATERAL WALKS
description: Level 1 lateral movement drill. Slow side stepping teaches foot placement, hip control, and trunk position without speed. Use for athletes with knee valgus, poor lateral hip control, or low-level balance deficits.

name: LATERAL SHUFFLES
description: Level 2 lateral locomotion drill. Shuffling adds rhythm and stance-width control while the athlete maintains a low athletic base. Use for court and field athletes learning controlled frontal-plane movement.

name: BAND RESISTED SHUFFLES
description: Level 3 resisted lateral drill. Band tension increases hip and trunk demand while the athlete maintains shuffle rhythm. Use for athletes who drift upright, cross their feet, or lose pelvic control.

name: CROSSOVER RUNS
description: Level 4 crossover coordination drill. Crossover action trains hip rotation and foot repositioning while moving laterally. Use for athletes preparing for curved runs, recovery steps, or defensive transitions.

name: SHUFFLE TO SPRINT
description: Level 5 transition drill. The movement changes from lateral shuffle to forward acceleration, training hip turn and reorientation. Use for athletes who pause or stand tall when changing from defense to sprint.

name: REACTIVE SHUFFLES
description: Level 6 reactive lateral drill. Cue-driven direction changes train braking and re-acceleration from a shuffle stance. Use for athletes who need lateral control under decision demand.

name: MIRROR SHUFFLES
description: Level 7 partner-reactive drill. The athlete matches an external mover, linking visual processing to lateral footwork. Use for court and field athletes who must stay organized while tracking an opponent.

name: CHAOS SHUFFLES
description: Level 8 advanced lateral agility drill. Unpredictable cues, resistance, or ball actions challenge lateral movement under unstable constraints. Use for advanced athletes preparing for competition-speed defensive movement.

name: WALK-IN CUTS
description: Level 1 cutting mechanics drill. Walking speed reduces load while the athlete learns plant-foot angle, hip position, and trunk lean. Use for FMS Score 1–2 athletes or early return-to-change-of-direction phases.

name: JOG-IN CUTS
description: Level 2 low-speed cutting drill. Jog approach adds manageable momentum while preserving technical control of the plant. Use for athletes who can walk through cuts but lose alignment at light speed.

name: 45° PLANT & GO
description: Level 3 angled reorientation drill. The 45-degree plant trains controlled redirection with lower braking demand than sharper cuts. Use for athletes learning to redirect without valgus collapse or trunk drift.

name: 45° RE-ACCELERATION CUTS
description: Level 4 re-acceleration drill. The cut is paired with immediate push-off to train braking-to-propulsion transfer. Use for athletes who plant safely but fail to exit the cut with intent.

name: BAND RESISTED CUTS
description: Level 5 resisted cutting drill. Band tension adds horizontal force and exposes trunk or hip leakage during the plant. Use for athletes who need stronger push-off mechanics after technical cuts are clean.

name: REACTIVE 45° CUTS
description: Level 6 reactive cutting drill. External cues delay direction selection and increase perception-action demand. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned 45-degree cuts are stable.

name: BALL REACTION CUTS
description: Level 7 ball-reactive cutting drill. Tracking or receiving the ball layers visual attention over plant mechanics and re-acceleration. Use for field and court athletes who cut cleanly in drills but break down with ball involvement.

name: SPORT-SPECIFIC CUTS
description: Level 8 transfer cutting drill. Stance, approach speed, cue, and exit angle match the athlete’s sport context. Use in performance phases after general cutting mechanics are reliable.

name: WALK-IN 90° CUTS
description: Level 1 right-angle cutting drill. Walking speed lowers braking load while the athlete learns foot placement and hip turn for a 90-degree change. Use for athletes who need technical exposure before sharper loaded cuts.

name: JOG-IN 90° CUTS
description: Level 2 low-speed right-angle drill. Jog approach adds momentum while keeping the plant manageable. Use for athletes who can walk the pattern but lose knee or trunk control with speed.

name: 90° PLANT & GO
description: Level 3 right-angle reorientation drill. The 90-degree plant increases braking demand and trains clean redirection off the outside leg. Use for athletes who need sharper change-of-direction mechanics before reactive work.

name: 90° RE-ACCELERATION CUTS
description: Level 4 right-angle exit drill. Immediate acceleration after the plant trains force transfer from braking into propulsion. Use for athletes who stop well but exit slowly or upright.

name: MULTI-CONE 90° CUTS
description: Level 5 sequencing drill. Multiple cones repeat the 90-degree cut and challenge consistency under fatigue and spacing constraints. Use for athletes who need technical repeatability before open agility.

name: REACTIVE 90° CUTS
description: Level 6 reactive right-angle drill. Cue-driven direction selection forces rapid deceleration and reorientation. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned 90-degree cuts are clean.

name: BALL REACTION CUTS
description: Level 7 ball-reactive right-angle drill. Ball tracking adds visual and timing demand while the athlete executes a sharp cut. Use for athletes whose cutting mechanics degrade when attention shifts to the ball.

name: OPEN SKILL 90° CUTS
description: Level 8 open-skill cutting drill. Defender, space, or game cue determines the 90-degree cut instead of a fixed cone. Use in performance phases when athletes need game-speed decision making.

name: WALK-IN TURNAROUNDS
description: Level 1 turnaround mechanics drill. Walking speed teaches hip turn, foot repositioning, and trunk control for 180-degree redirection. Use for athletes who need low-load exposure to shuttle mechanics.

name: SHUTTLE TURNS
description: Level 2 shuttle technique drill. Repeated turnarounds train plant-foot placement and low-hip braking at controlled speed. Use for athletes who stand tall or spin through direction changes.

name: PRO AGILITY 5-10-5
description: Level 3 structured COD drill. The fixed distances constrain acceleration, deceleration, and 180-degree turn mechanics. Use for athletes who need measurable change-of-direction practice before reactive shuttles.

name: 180° SPRINT RETURNS
description: Level 4 sprint-return drill. Higher approach speed increases braking demand before the athlete re-accelerates back. Use for athletes who can turn in shuttles but lose posture under sprint entry.

name: RESISTED SHUTTLES
description: Level 5 resisted COD drill. External resistance increases force demand through the turn and exit. Use for athletes who need stronger re-acceleration after stable 180-degree mechanics.

name: REACTIVE SHUTTLES
description: Level 6 reactive shuttle drill. Cue-driven turn timing forces the athlete to brake and re-accelerate without knowing the stop point. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned shuttle work is consistent.

name: MIRROR SHUTTLES
description: Level 7 opponent-reactive drill. Matching a partner links visual processing, braking, and 180-degree re-acceleration. Use for athletes who need shuttle mechanics under opponent pressure.

name: CHAOS SHUTTLES
description: Level 8 advanced shuttle drill. Random cues, variable distances, and competitive pressure challenge turn mechanics under game-speed uncertainty. Use for advanced athletes preparing for high-demand change-of-direction environments.

name: SINGLE STEP LADDER
description: Level 1 foot-placement drill. The ladder constrains step location and trains basic rhythm at low intensity. Use for athletes who need coordination and foot awareness before faster agility work.

name: DOUBLE STEP LADDER
description: Level 2 rhythm coordination drill. Two contacts per box increase cadence control and limb timing. Use for athletes who rush footwork or cannot maintain consistent step rhythm.

name: IN-IN-OUT-OUT
description: Level 3 lateral coordination drill. The pattern alternates narrow and wide foot positions to train hip control and foot speed. Use for athletes learning lateral foot repositioning before shuffles and cuts.

name: ICKEY SHUFFLE
description: Level 4 ladder transition drill. The Ickey pattern combines lateral entry, crossover timing, and forward progression. Use for athletes who need coordinated footwork transitions without high braking load.

name: LATERAL LADDER SERIES
description: Level 5 frontal-plane ladder drill. Lateral patterns constrain stance width and rhythm while the athlete moves side to side. Use for athletes preparing for shuffle and defensive footwork progressions.

name: CROSSOVER LADDER SERIES
description: Level 6 crossover footwork drill. Crossover patterns train hip rotation, foot clearance, and reorientation inside a constrained grid. Use for athletes who need cleaner crossover mechanics before open-field movement.

name: REACTIVE LADDER DRILLS
description: Level 7 reactive footwork drill. External cues change pattern or direction and force rapid foot placement decisions. Use when ladder mechanics are automatic and the athlete needs cognitive load.

name: CHAOS LADDER DRILLS
description: Level 8 advanced coordination drill. Randomized patterns, cues, or partner pressure challenge footwork without a predictable sequence. Use sparingly for advanced athletes as a neural-speed and coordination exposure.

name: LINEAR CONE RUNS
description: Level 1 cone-running drill. Straight cone spacing constrains stride path and teaches controlled acceleration and deceleration. Use for athletes learning to run through targets without drifting or overstriding.

name: BOX DRILLS
description: Level 2 multi-directional cone drill. The box layout introduces forward, lateral, and backward movement in a predictable sequence. Use for athletes who need basic directional vocabulary before sharper agility drills.

name: T-DRILLS
description: Level 3 structured agility drill. The T-shape combines sprinting, shuffling, backpedaling, and braking in one fixed pattern. Use for athletes developing general COD mechanics with clear constraints.

name: L-DRILLS
description: Level 4 curved COD drill. The L-pattern trains tight turns, body lean, and re-acceleration around cones. Use for athletes who need transition from linear sprinting into angled change of direction.

name: W-DRILLS
description: Level 5 repeated-angle drill. The W-pattern repeats diagonal cuts and re-acceleration under predictable spacing. Use for athletes who need cutting consistency across multiple contacts.

name: STAR DRILLS
description: Level 6 multi-vector cone drill. The star layout exposes acceleration and deceleration in several directions from a central point. Use for athletes who need controlled multi-directional movement before reactive cone work.

name: REACTIVE CONE DRILLS
description: Level 7 reactive cone drill. Cue-driven cone selection links visual processing to acceleration, braking, and reorientation. Use in late return-to-sport phases when planned cone drills are stable.

name: CHAOS CONE DRILLS
description: Level 8 open-pattern cone drill. Random cone calls and variable routes challenge decision making, foot placement, and speed control. Use for advanced athletes preparing for unpredictable field or court movement.

name: VISUAL CUE WALKS
description: Level 1 perception-action drill. Walking speed lets the athlete pair visual information with movement choice under low load. Use for athletes early in agility retraining or after concussion-related reactivity limitations.

name: VISUAL CUE SHUFFLES
description: Level 2 visual-reaction shuffle drill. Lateral movement adds footwork demand while visual cues determine direction. Use for athletes who can shuffle technically but need low-speed decision exposure.

name: COACH POINT DRILLS
description: Level 3 coach-cued agility drill. Pointing cues create simple external direction changes without complex stimulus processing. Use for athletes progressing from pre-planned agility to reactive movement.

name: COLOR REACTION DRILLS
description: Level 4 visual discrimination drill. Color cues require stimulus identification before movement selection. Use for athletes who move well but need better reaction accuracy under cognitive load.

name: LIGHT REACTION DRILLS
description: Level 5 high-speed visual drill. Light cues reduce anticipation and demand fast perception-to-movement coupling. Use for athletes who need objective reaction exposure without opponent complexity.

name: AUDIO REACTION DRILLS
description: Level 6 auditory reaction drill. Sound cues remove visual direction preview and challenge start timing. Use for athletes who need reaction speed from whistle, clap, or sport-specific audio cues.

name: RANDOM REACTIVE AGILITY
description: Level 7 randomized agility drill. Randomized cues prevent pattern memorization and force real-time movement selection. Use in late preparation phases when planned agility no longer challenges decision quality.

name: OPEN SKILL AGILITY
description: Level 8 open-skill agility drill. Movement direction, timing, and speed are dictated by opponent, ball, or game context. Use in performance phases to bridge controlled agility into sport transfer.

name: PARTNER FOLLOW WALKS
description: Level 1 partner-tracking drill. Walking pace lets the athlete track an external mover while maintaining posture and spacing. Use for athletes new to reactive agility or returning from balance deficits.

name: PARTNER SHUFFLES
description: Level 2 partner lateral drill. The athlete matches a partner’s side-to-side movement while controlling stance width and foot placement. Use for athletes learning visual tracking during defensive movement.

name: MIRROR SHUFFLES
description: Level 3 mirror lateral drill. Mirroring links perception, braking, and lateral re-acceleration against a live mover. Use for athletes who shuffle well alone but lose timing against an opponent.

name: MIRROR SPRINTS
description: Level 4 mirror acceleration drill. Sprint mirroring increases speed and demands rapid acceleration response to partner movement. Use for field athletes who need chase, closeout, or separation mechanics.

name: MIRROR COD
description: Level 5 mirror change-of-direction drill. Partner movement dictates cut timing and angle, forcing reactive braking and reorientation. Use for athletes who need COD mechanics under opponent-driven constraints.

name: REACTIVE MIRROR DRILLS
description: Level 6 reactive mirror drill. Added cues or constraints prevent anticipation and sharpen perception-action coupling. Use in late return-to-sport phases when standard mirroring becomes predictable.

name: OPEN SKILL MIRROR DRILLS
description: Level 7 open-skill partner drill. The live mover creates variable speed, angle, and deception demands. Use for court and field athletes preparing for sport-specific tracking and response.

name: COMPETITIVE MIRROR AGILITY
description: Level 8 competitive agility drill. Scoring, time pressure, or win-loss constraints raise intent and decision stress. Use for advanced athletes who need game-speed agility with accountability.

name: SL STICK LANDINGS
description: Level 1 single-leg landing drill. The stick phase trains foot, knee, hip, and trunk alignment after one-leg impact. Use for athletes with FMS asymmetry or post-injury landing-control deficits.

name: SL HOP TO STICK
description: Level 2 single-leg deceleration drill. The hop adds flight while the stick phase controls braking and alignment. Use for athletes returning from ankle, knee, or hip injury after static single-leg balance is stable.

name: SL LATERAL HOPS
description: Level 3 frontal-plane hop drill. Lateral hopping increases hip-abductor demand and edge control during one-leg contacts. Use for athletes preparing for shuffling, cutting, and lateral deceleration.

name: SL DIAGONAL HOPS
description: Level 4 multi-vector hop drill. Diagonal hopping blends forward and lateral force and challenges foot placement. Use for athletes who own linear and lateral hops but struggle with angled landings.

name: SL CUT & HOLD
description: Level 5 single-leg cutting drill. The plant-and-hold pattern trains one-leg braking without immediate re-acceleration. Use for athletes who need to control knee and pelvis position before faster cuts.

name: SL RE-ACCELERATION CUTS
description: Level 6 single-leg exit drill. The cut is paired with immediate push-off to train braking-to-propulsion transfer from one leg. Use for athletes who can hold the cut but cannot exit with speed.

name: REACTIVE SL CUTS
description: Level 7 reactive single-leg COD drill. External cues force rapid plant selection and re-acceleration from one-leg support. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned single-leg cuts are stable.

name: MULTI-PLANAR SL AGILITY
description: Level 8 advanced single-leg agility drill. Multi-planar directions challenge projection, braking, and reorientation from one-leg support. Use only for advanced athletes with clean landings and no pain response.

name: BAND MARCHES
description: Level 1 resisted patterning drill. Band resistance adds horizontal force while the athlete practices posture and knee drive at low speed. Use for athletes learning acceleration mechanics before resisted running.

name: BAND SHUFFLES
description: Level 2 resisted lateral drill. Band tension increases hip and trunk demand during controlled side-to-side movement. Use for athletes who lose stance width or posture during lateral shuffles.

name: BAND CUTS
description: Level 3 resisted cutting drill. Elastic resistance exposes trunk leakage and foot-placement errors during the plant. Use for athletes who own low-speed cuts and need stronger exit mechanics.

name: SLED SHUFFLES
description: Level 4 loaded lateral drill. The sled adds measurable resistance while the athlete maintains lateral posture and foot rhythm. Use for athletes who need frontal-plane strength integrated into agility work.

name: RESISTED COD RUNS
description: Level 5 resisted change-of-direction drill. External load raises braking and re-acceleration demand through planned cuts. Use for athletes who maintain clean technique but need greater force output.

name: HEAVY RESISTED COD
description: Level 6 heavy-force COD drill. Heavier resistance slows movement and emphasizes force production through the plant and exit. Use in strength-power phases for athletes with stable joints and clean mechanics.

name: CONTRAST COD DRILLS
description: Level 7 contrast agility drill. Resisted cuts paired with unloaded cuts use potentiation to sharpen re-acceleration. Use for trained athletes who can preserve mechanics under both loaded and unloaded conditions.

name: REACTIVE RESISTED AGILITY
description: Level 8 reactive resisted drill. Cue-driven movement under resistance challenges force production and decision making together. Use for advanced athletes after planned resisted COD work is consistent.

name: FORWARD-BACKWARD RUNS
description: Level 1 directional-transition drill. Alternating forward and backward running teaches basic reorientation and posture control. Use for athletes who need low-complexity direction changes before lateral patterns.

name: LATERAL-TO-FORWARD RUNS
description: Level 2 transition agility drill. The drill changes from lateral movement to forward acceleration, training hip turn and first-step orientation. Use for athletes who pause when moving from defense to attack.

name: TRIANGLE DRILLS
description: Level 3 angled agility drill. The triangle layout exposes acceleration and deceleration across predictable angles. Use for athletes learning to redirect without the complexity of open cues.

name: STAR DRILLS
description: Level 4 multi-vector agility drill. The star pattern trains movement out of and back into a central base across several directions. Use for athletes who need controlled multi-directional exposure before random drills.

name: CROSS DRILLS
description: Level 5 directional-control drill. The cross layout combines forward, backward, and lateral movement with repeated stops. Use for athletes who need braking and re-acceleration across simple sport-like vectors.

name: RANDOM MOVEMENT DRILLS
description: Level 6 randomized agility drill. Random routes reduce anticipation and force the athlete to organize footwork in real time. Use when planned multi-directional drills no longer expose decision or control errors.

name: REACTIVE MULTI-DIRECTIONAL AGILITY
description: Level 7 reactive multi-planar drill. External cues dictate direction, distance, and timing across multiple movement planes. Use in late return-to-sport phases for athletes who need agility under uncertainty.

name: CHAOS AGILITY SERIES
description: Level 8 advanced open-agility drill. Unpredictable stimuli, opponent movement, and variable space challenge perception, braking, and re-acceleration together. Use for advanced athletes preparing for game-speed movement demands.

name: 5-10-5 SHUTTLE
description: Level 1 performance COD benchmark. The fixed shuttle distances quantify acceleration, braking, and 180-degree turn mechanics. Use for athletes who need a standardized COD test and technical reference point.

name: T-TEST
description: Level 2 multi-directional benchmark drill. The T-test combines sprinting, shuffling, and backpedaling under fixed spacing. Use for athletes who need structured assessment of general agility qualities.

name: L-DRILL
description: Level 3 curved COD benchmark. The L-pattern trains tight turns, body lean, and re-acceleration around cones. Use for athletes who need measurable curved change-of-direction exposure.

name: Y-REACTIVE DRILL
description: Level 4 reactive fork drill. The Y shape delays direction selection and forces the athlete to react into one of two exits. Use for athletes transitioning from planned cone drills into reactive agility.

name: REACTIVE SHUTTLE SERIES
description: Level 5 reactive shuttle complex. Variable shuttle distances and cues train braking and re-acceleration without predictable timing. Use in late return-to-sport phases after planned shuttles are technically sound.

name: SPORT-SPECIFIC AGILITY
description: Level 6 transfer agility drill. The drill matches the athlete’s sport stance, cue source, space, and movement angles. Use in performance phases once general COD mechanics are reliable.

name: SMALL SIDED REACTION DRILLS
description: Level 7 competitive reaction drill. Small-sided constraints create live perception, decision, and movement demands with limited space. Use for advanced athletes who need agility transfer under sport-like pressure.

name: CHAOS GAME-SPEED AGILITY
description: Level 8 advanced open-skill drill. Full-speed unpredictable play constraints challenge acceleration, deceleration, cutting, and reactive decision making together. Use only for athletes with clean mechanics, high tissue tolerance, and full return-to-sport readiness.
